We provide purpose-driven work in a safe and inclusive environment, and we live by our North Star .  One Full-Time Opportunity.

 This position plays a key role in assessing the impacts of significant unusual transactions, assessing new accounting standards and regulations, and preparing the Company’s quarterly and annual financial statements.

 Advising on technical accounting matters and preparing supporting memos on an ad hoc basis, as required

 Preparing or reviewing certain notes and supporting working papers to the quarterly and annual financial statements

 Monitoring IFRS developments and preparing a memo to the Audit Committee summarizing significant changes to IFRS, on a quarterly basis

 performing various other SOX controls, as required
 What you will bring to the role: 
 Education & Experience: 
 Post-Secondary Degree in Business, Finance or Accounting
 A professional accounting designation
 Experience working with IFRS
 A minimum of 3 years of post-designation accounting experience.
 Past experience working as part of a Financial Reporting team, Experience working for a publicly listed company is an asset
 Experience with Oracle is an asset
 Experience with US GAAP is an asset
 Proficiency in excel and Microsoft Office Suite

 Hybrid: work from home on Mondays and Fridays and in the office Tuesdays through Thursdays.

Who we are
 About Stripe
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. 
 About the team
 The Risk team builds trust, an essential ingredient for Stripe’s mission to increase the GDP of the internet. We make it possible for millions of businesses to access and use Stripe’s financial infrastructure while protecting our users, financial partners, and the broader ecosystem from harm.
 Risk sits at the center of our users’ and Stripe’s ability to grow safely. We help legitimate businesses access Stripe’s financial services, provide credit to creditworthy businesses, and increasingly help users manage their own risk. We also prevent fraud and financial crime, manage Stripe’s credit exposure, meet our obligations to regulators and financial partners, and enable Stripe’s product teams to launch and grow products safely. To do this, we set the policies and standards that guide how Stripe manages risk and develop the advanced AI, infrastructure, and product experiences that put them into practice for Stripe and our users.
 At Stripe’s scale—$1.9 trillion in annual payment volume, equivalent to 1.6% of global GDP, processed across millions of businesses—we face risk problems no other company has encountered. The opportunities and complexities are only growing as AI reshapes what is possible, Stripe expands its product suite, regulators raise their expectations, and we support more businesses in more countries.
 What you’ll do
 As a Staff Product Manager on the Risk team, you will lead cross-Risk and cross-Stripe initiatives that fundamentally change how Stripe and our users manage risk. You will identify the most important opportunities that cut across Risk’s infrastructure and products, define solutions to our most ambiguous problems, and drive execution from early technical shaping through delivery and adoption.
 You will operate as a product counterpart to Risk’s senior technical leaders. You will shape infrastructure and product direction across Risk, connect work that would otherwise remain fragmented, and help product teams across Stripe build on Risk’s capabilities. You will remain deeply engaged in the work, helping teams navigate difficult technical and product decisions.
 Responsibilities
 Identify high-leverage problems that cut across teams, turn ambiguity into clear product and technical direction, and establish measurable outcomes.
 Lead major cross-Risk and cross-Stripe initiatives from initial shaping through delivery, adoption, and iteration.
 Lead changes in Risk’s approach to using data and AI to accurately identify and mitigate risk at scale.
 Partner deeply with engineering, data science, and machine learning leaders to shape architecture, data foundations, models, APIs, and product experiences.
 Help product teams across Stripe build on Risk’s capabilities quickly and effectively while guiding Risk teams toward coherent, reusable infrastructure and product decisions.
 Build alignment among teams with different goals and constraints, resolve difficult tradeoffs, and drive progress without relying on formal authority.
 Who you are 
 We’re looking for an exceptional product leader who combines strong technical judgment with product insight, strategic range, and executional rigor. You identify important problems before they become obvious, bring clarity to deeply ambiguous spaces, and mobilize teams around solutions that work across products, organizations, and time horizons. You are deeply curious and stay at the forefront of advances in AI and technology, finding practical ways to apply them to our most challenging problems.
 You move fluently from defining multi-year strategy to driving the details of execution. You build alignment and lead transformational work across teams without direct management authority.  The University of Ottawa (uOttawa) invites applications for a tenure-track Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader position in cancer research and/or cell therapy, aligned with the Government of Canada strategic priority area of Health. This position is associated with the Canada Impact+ Research Chair in Next-Generation Translational T Cell Immunotherapies in the Faculty of Medicine, as part of the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairs of Canada Program (formerly Canada Impact+ Research Chairs Program). 
 We seek candidates whose research program advances the understanding, development, or clinical translation of immune-based therapies for human disease, including cancer and other conditions where immune modulation offers transformative potential. Areas of expertise may include, but are not limited to, immunology, cellular therapies, synthetic biology, bioengineering, systems biology, computational and AI-enabled approaches or translational medicine. The successful candidate will leverage our established strengths in immunology, cancer research, translational medicine, and biomanufacturing to build an ambitious research program that spans basic and translational biomedical science.
 The Impact+ Emerging Leader will join the Department of Biochemistry, Microbiology and Immunology (BMI) in the Faculty of Medicine , a vibrant and collaborative research environment with internationally recognized strengths in immunology, infection and immunity, cancer biology, molecular medicine, and translational biomedical research. The successful candidate will have opportunities to build strong collaborations across the University of Ottawa, its affiliated research institutes and hospital partners, and a broad network of national and international collaborators. Candidates whose research complements and expands existing departmental expertise, while fostering interdisciplinary partnerships and training the next generation of scientists and clinician-scientists, are particularly encouraged to apply. The University of Ottawa offers a uniquely collaborative ecosystem that supports innovation at the interface of fundamental discovery, technology development, and clinical translation.
 uOttawa is ranked fifth in research intensity in 2025 and is renowned for pioneering discoveries across multiple disciplines. Several of our research centers and institutes rank among the top 100 globally, including the top six in Canada.  
 Located in Canada’s vibrant capital and proud to be the world’s largest bilingual (English and French) university, uOttawa is minutes away from federal and other government institutions, several national agencies, embassies, international organizations, and connected to the thriving high-tech sector. We are committed to building partnerships across Canada and internationally and fostering innovation and knowledge mobilization in areas of significant social and economic impact.  
 About the Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders Program   
 The Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairs of Canada Program is a very prestigious, one-time initiative designed to support universities in attracting world-leading researchers whose work addresses critical national and global challenges. The program also includes Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders awards, a $120M investment to help institutions recruit internationally based early career researchers to Canada.
 The Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders award provides $100,000 per year over six years, with the possibility of a six-year funded extension at the same yearly amount, subject to program conditions. 
 T he Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader must be recruited within the same strategic priority area as the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairholder, but the early career researcher (ECR) and the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairholder don't necessarily need to be in the same discipline or research field or be aligned with the same federal research funding agency. The ECR nominees are expected to have an independent program of research, with potential for impact through collaborations with, but not limited to, the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairholders. Institutions may include support for the ECR in their research infrastructure request to the Canada Foundation for Innovation (CFI) through the Impact+ Research Infrastructure fund associated with the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair .

 Only candidates who are internationally based (both working and residing outside of Canada) when the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair is accepted are eligible.  research-related appointments are defined as those where the individual has the autonomy to conduct research independently (including assistant professor); and

 Before you apply: This is a fully remote role open to candidates anywhere in Canada. We’re hiring for an existing, open position. During live conversations, please don’t use AI to generate responses unless invited to do so. 
 The Work You’ll Do
 In your first few weeks, you’ll get to know Acuity’s business, current accounting systems, processes, and controls, working alongside our Controller and accounting team to understand how things work today and where we can improve.
 We’re working toward a five-business-day close, and you’ll play an important role in helping us get there.
 Own complex accounting work 
 You’ll own significant areas of the accounting cycle, including complex journal entries and reconciliations, month-end and year-end close, financial reporting, and audit support. You’ll also review reconciliations and supporting schedules prepared by the team, investigate unusual items, and ensure the close is complete and ready for Controller review.
 When accounting questions are complex or something doesn’t reconcile, you’ll dig into the details, investigate root causes, and use sound judgment to recommend the right path forward. Your work will help us build a faster, more reliable close supported by strong processes and controls.
 Strengthen revenue accounting and reporting 
 You’ll provide senior-level review and oversight of revenue accounting, including revenue recognition, deferred revenue, reconciliations, and related reporting. Working with teammates responsible for invoicing, receivables, and recurring revenue schedules, you’ll connect business activity with accounting records.
 You’ll review accounting outputs, investigate discrepancies, and resolve complex or unusual transactions. You’ll help ensure revenue is recognized appropriately, supporting schedules reconcile to the general ledger, and financial and business reporting is accurate and reliable..
 Turn accounting information into reliable financial insight 
 You’ll help ensure the accounting information behind our financial and business reporting is accurate, consistent, and reliable, including the preparation and reconciliation of recurring revenue metrics.
 You’ll contribute accounting insights and historical context to financial analysis, budgeting, and forecasting, helping the business make informed decisions. You’ll also support cash management through short-term cash forecasting, cash flow variance analysis, and visibility into upcoming cash requirements.
 Help modernize our accounting systems 
 We’re preparing to move to a new accounting platform. You’ll contribute your accounting expertise to the transition, from defining requirements and improving workflows to data validation, testing, and migration.
 You’ll also have opportunities to take ownership of meaningful improvements that make our systems and processes more efficient, reliable, and easier to use.
 Improve how Accounting works 
 You’ll look beyond your own responsibilities to identify recurring problems, unnecessary manual work, and opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen controls, and use automation or AI thoughtfully.
 You’ll help turn those opportunities into practical improvements, while strengthening documentation, sharing knowledge, and building better coverage across the team.
 The goal is an accounting function that spends less time moving information around and more time on the work where expertise and judgment matter.
 Who You’ll Work With and How
 You’ll report to our Controller and work alongside a small team of accountants. You’ll have meaningful ownership of your work while sharing knowledge, solving problems together, and helping strengthen how Accounting operates.
 Accounting connects to almost every part of Acuity, so you’ll work closely with people across the business:
 Your Accounting teammates , to work through complex questions, share expertise, strengthen coverage, and improve how the team works.
 Revenue Operations , to connect contracts, billing, revenue, and the information that supports accurate financial reporting.
 People & Culture , on payroll, employee-related accounting, and the processes that connect our teams.
 Leaders and budget owners , to understand the context behind transactions, resolve accounting questions, and support reliable financial information.
 External partners , including auditors and other Finance partners, to support reporting, compliance, and audit readiness.
 You’ll work with a high degree of independence, but not in isolation. You’ll know when to make decisions, when to bring others in, and how to build trust through clear communication, sound judgment, and reliable follow-through.
 What Success Looks Like
 In your first three months, you’ll build an understanding of Acuity’s business, accounting cycle, systems, and controls. You’ll begin taking ownership of key accounting responsibilities, building relationships across the business, and identifying opportunities to improve how work gets done.
 By six months, you’ll independently own significant areas of the accounting cycle, confidently work through complex reconciliations and accounting questions, and identify issues before they become problems. You’ll also begin turning improvement opportunities into practical changes.
 By the end of your first year, you’ll be a trusted source of accounting expertise, handling complex work with minimal guidance and contributing improvements beyond your own responsibilities. Your impact will be visible in stronger processes, better controls, and greater shared knowledge and coverage across Accounting.
 How You’ll Succeed
 You’ll likely thrive here if you:
 Take ownership. You follow work through to resolution, surface issues early, and take responsibility for accurate, reliable outcomes.
 Look beyond the numbers. You investigate discrepancies, ask questions, and connect the dots to understand what’s really happening.
 Balance judgment with momentum. You respect accounting standards and controls while knowing when to make decisions, move forward, or bring others in.
 Look for better ways of working. Y ou notice unnecessary complexity and manual effort, finding practical opportunities to improve processes, systems, and controls.
 Share what you know. You document your work, offer guidance, and help build stronger knowledge and coverage across Accounting.
 Use technology thoughtfully. You explore how systems, automation, and AI can improve your work, applying the same judgment and care you’d bring to any accounting decision.
 Are comfortable building while doing. You work effectively as processes evolve, bringing structure to your own work while helping strengthen how Accounting operates.
 As the Finance function evolves, you’ll have opportunities to deepen your expertise, take on broader ownership, and contribute to larger systems and process improvements.
 Experience That Will Help You Hit the Ground Running
 You’ll bring strong technical accounting expertise, sound judgment, and the ability to independently own complex work. Your experience will include:
 Independently owning significant areas of month-end and year-end close, including journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, working papers, and general ledger accounting.
 Preparing or supporting financial reporting, ensuring the underlying accounting records are accurate, complete, and well supported.
 Working across revenue recognition, invoicing, receivables, or other core accounting activities, with an understanding of how they connect through the accounting cycle.
 Investigating complex accounting questions and discrepancies, applying accounting principles and professional judgment to determine the right path forward.
 Supporting external audits and maintaining strong documentation, controls, and audit readiness.
 Improving accounting processes, workflows, or systems to reduce manual work, strengthen reliability, and make the work more efficient.
 Working independently in evolving environments, knowing when to make decisions, collaborate, or escalate.

 How We Support You
 Transparent compensation. A salary between $95,000 - $105,000 CAD, aligned to role scope, experience, and internal equity.
 Learning that grows with you. A $3,000 annual learning budget to invest in your development, whether that’s deepening your accounting expertise, building new technical skills, or exploring new areas of interest.
 Shared success. Access to employee stock options, so you share in the value you help create.
 Remote-first work. Fully remote within Canada, with up to six weeks per year to work internationally.
 Time to rest and reset. Self-directed vacation (most teammates take 4–6 weeks annually), monthly Acuity Days (a collective Friday off), plus a two-week company-wide closure each December.
 Comprehensive care. Health benefits from day one for you and your dependents.
 Future-focused support. A 2% GRSP matching program to help you plan ahead.
 Support for growing families. A 16-week parental leave top-up beyond EI, available to all parents.
 What Happens After You Apply

 Our interviews are two-way conversations. We want to understand your career, abilities, and goals, and help you assess whether this opportunity and team are the right fit for you. 
 Steps in the Process

 Application Review. A real person reviews your application for potential fit.
 Intro Conversation. A conversation with a member of our Talent team to learn about your career journey, what you’re looking for next, and to introduce you to Acuity, Casper, and the role.
 Conversation with the Manager. You’ll meet our Controller to explore the accounting work you’ve owned, how you approach complex problems, and the decisions you’ve made along the way. If you have an example of real work you’re proud of and can share, bring it along. It could be a process you’ve improved or a way you’ve used technology, automation, or AI to work more effectively. No need to prepare anything new or formal. It’s an opportunity to share how you approached the work, the judgment you applied, and what you learned.
 Team Conversations. You’ll meet a few of the people you’d work with closely to explore how you collaborate, solve problems, and improve ways of working, while getting a better feel for what working together would be like.
 Decision. The hiring manager reviews feedback from the interview team and typically makes a decision within 2 to 4 business days.
 Offer & Reference Checks. If it’s a match, we’ll move to references and a formal offer.
 Life at Acuity Insights
 We’re a remote-first team of 135+ people, built around trust, flexibility, and giving people meaningful ownership of their work.
 Remote-first doesn’t mean working in isolation. We collaborate closely across teams, communicate thoughtfully across time zones, and create intentional opportunities to connect, while protecting the flexibility and focus that make remote work valuable.
 Day to day, you can expect:
 High trust and autonomy in how you get your work done.
 Thoughtful, async-friendly communication across a distributed team.
 Opportunities to share ideas and perspectives that help inform our direction.
 Colleagues who are generous with their expertise, challenge thinking, and learn from one another.
 A culture of curiosity, continuous learning, and thoughtful experimentation, including how we use AI.
 A sustainable approach to work that values impact over performative busyness.
 As we grow, we’re deliberate about evolving how we work without adding process for process’s sake. We want people to have the clarity, context, relationships, and room to make good decisions, challenge assumptions, and contribute to work that matters.
 About Acuity Insights
 At Acuity Insights, we build research-backed technology that helps higher education institutions better understand people, make informed decisions, and support learner development.
 We believe people are more than their grades, and that human potential can be understood, nurtured, and developed throughout the educational journey.

Our Casper situational judgment test, developed by researchers at McMaster University, has been completed by over 1 million applicants and is backed by nearly 20 years of research.

By combining research, technology, and responsible AI, we aim to help institutions make better decisions, create more meaningful learning experiences, and support people in reaching their potential.
 We’re at a point in our evolution where the work we do today is helping shape what’s possible tomorrow. And the people who join us will have an opportunity to contribute to that future.

 Primary Purpose   
 The Financial Coordinator supports the administration and coordination of financial operations for assigned departments, faculties, portfolios, institutes, or administrative units. The role contributes to accurate, timely, and compliant financial operations by administering financial processes, maintaining financial information, supporting monitoring and reporting activities, and providing information and guidance on established financial requirements.  
 Within the Faculty of Mathematics, the Financial Coordinator supports financial operations for assigned departments and units, including operating, endowment, and research funds and Faculty-specific financial activities. The role provides financial process support to Faculty stakeholders and supports the administration of Math-specific funding and financial requirements within established University policies and procedures.  
 Key Accountabilities   
 Faculty of Mathematics Financial Support   
 Coordinates financial activities and requirements for units within the Faculty of Mathematics.  
 Supports the administration and monitoring of operating and research funds, including maintaining information on funding sources, commitments, key dates, and financial activity.  
 Supports Faculty-specific financial activities, including the administration of Math Endowment Fund claims, invoices, project funding, student claims, and related records.  
 Provides information and guidance to Faculty stakeholders regarding established financial processes, documentation requirements, account coding, approvals, and transaction requirements.  
 Maintains tracking information and supporting documentation for Faculty-specific financial activities and identifies matters requiring follow-up or escalation.  
 Supports the consistent application of University financial policies, procedures, and internal controls to Faculty-specific activities.  
 Financial Operations   
 Coordinates and administers financial transactions, including expense reimbursements, purchasing transactions, invoices, journal entries, deposits, transfers, and related documentation.  
 Reviews financial transactions for completeness, accuracy, appropriate approvals, supporting documentation, and compliance with University policies and procedures.  
 Investigates transaction discrepancies and coordinates corrections or resolutions as required.  
 Maintains accurate financial records, supporting documentation, and audit trails.  
 Supports procurement activities, including reviewing purchasing requirements, coordinating purchases, and ensuring compliance with applicable procurement policies, procedures, and delegated authorities.  
 Assists with month-end and year-end financial activities.  
 Provides information and guidance to stakeholders regarding established financial systems, processes, and requirements.  
 Financial Monitoring and Reporting   
 Monitors financial activity within assigned portfolios and identifies unusual transactions, variances, deficits, commitments, or outstanding items requiring follow-up.  
 Extracts, compiles, validates, and organizes financial information from University systems.  
 Prepares regular and ad hoc financial reports to support operational requirements and decision-making.  
 Maintains information related to budgets, expenditures, commitments, and financial activity.  
 Supports forecasting and budget administration processes through data collection, reconciliation, and reporting activities.  
 Financial Controls and Compliance   
 Applies established financial controls, procedures, and administrative practices to assigned financial activities.  
 Conducts reviews and reconciliations to ensure accuracy and integrity of financial records.  
 Supports compliance with University policies, procedures, sponsor requirements, and applicable financial guidelines.  
 Identifies discrepancies, control gaps, or process concerns and escalates issues as appropriate.  
 Supports internal and external audit activities through the preparation and provision of financial information and documentation.  
 Financial Support and Improvement  
 Provides information and guidance to faculty, staff, managers, and other stakeholders regarding established financial processes, procedures, documentation requirements, and transaction requirements.  
 Supports stakeholders in resolving routine financial issues and discrepancies and escalates complex or non-routine matters as appropriate.  
 Builds effective working relationships with stakeholders and central administrative units.  
 Supports consistent application of financial procedures and practices through information sharing and guidance.  
 Identifies opportunities to improve financial processes and administrative practices and communicates recommendations to the appropriate level.  
 Participates in the testing, implementation, and enhancement of financial systems, tools, and processes.  
 Contributes to special projects and initiatives supporting financial operations as assigned.  
 Required Qualifications   
 Education   
 Undergraduate degree or post-secondary diploma in accounting, finance, commerce, business administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.  
 Experience   
 1 to 2 years of progressively responsible experience supporting financial administration, accounting, reconciliations, reporting, budgeting support, or related financial functions.  
 Experience working with financial systems, data analysis tools, and reporting applications.  
 Experience interpreting and applying financial policies, procedures, and administrative guidelines.  
 Experience working within a large, complex organization is an asset.  
 Knowledge/Skills/Abilities   
 Working knowledge of accounting principles and financial administration practices.  
 Ability to apply established financial policies, procedures, controls, and administrative practices to assigned activities.  
 Analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to review financial information and identify discrepancies or issues requiring follow-up.  
 Organizational and prioritization skills with the ability to manage multiple financial activities, deadlines, and competing demands.  
 Effective communication and stakeholder relationship management skills.  
 Ability to exercise judgment in resolving routine financial issues and determining when matters require escalation.  
 Ability to work independently within established procedures while effectively collaborating with others.  
 Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy in financial records and transactions.  
 Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and financial information systems.

 The Role
 ServiceCentral is hiring Partnership & Growth Associates to win new customers and grow the ones we bring in. New business is the priority here, and prospecting is not something you fit around the edges of your week, it is the heart of the job.

You will build real product depth, get hands-on coaching from people who have done this work themselves, and have experienced support in the room when a deal gets complex. What we are looking for in return is drive, curiosity, and a genuine appetite for hitting a number.
 What You Will Own
 Pipeline generation and conversion
 Generate qualified pipeline through outbound calling, email sequences, and social outreach across assigned campaigns, verticals, and territories
 Sustain consistent, high-volume prospecting activity as the anchor of your week
 Manage and qualify inbound leads with fast, accurate follow-up and correct routing
 Research accounts and stakeholders so outreach is personalised rather than generic
 Run discovery conversations using our qualification framework, and deliver online product demonstrations
 Close new business against a quarterly quota
 Hand off opportunities above your authority to Specialists, Managers, or Directors with full context, and earn sourced-pipeline credit
 Route opportunities on the other platform to your counterpart owner, and earn referral credit
 Account ownership
 Own the full commercial relationship for your assigned portfolio of accounts
 Maintain a defined contact cadence so no owned account drifts without engagement
 Execute standard renewals cleanly and on time
 Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities, closing the simple ones and pulling in a Manager or Director on the rest
 Monitor account health signals and flag at-risk relationships early, before they become recoveries
 Execute defined save plays on accounts showing risk
 Onboarding and time to value
 Own commercial handoff and welcome communications that set clear expectations
 Coordinate onboarding with Solutions and Support so customers reach value quickly
 Track time-to-first-value on your accounts and intervene when it slips
 Act on or route expansion signals that surface during onboarding
 Revenue integrity
 Audit subscription billing on your accounts to prevent revenue leakage
 Monitor involuntary churn signals (failed and declined charges) and drive resolution within 24 hours
 Reconcile the billing platform against internal records so MRR reporting is accurate
 Verify plan changes (upgrades, downgrades, cancellations) are executed correctly before a customer notices an error
 Surface systemic billing patterns to your Manager rather than fixing the same problem repeatedly
 Enablement and team support
 Provide day-to-day support on larger accounts held by senior colleagues: routine maintenance, data updates, configuration changes, and low-complexity requests
 Absorb repeatable work so senior capacity stays on new business and strategic pursuits
 Create and maintain customer-facing Knowledge Base and self-service content that drives adoption and reduces inbound volume
 Verify release notes for accuracy and customer clarity before publication
 Support go-to-market materials and campaign content for upsell and cross-sell motions
 Support trade shows and events: booth materials, collateral, demo environment readiness, on-site coordination, and lead capture with follow-up
 Systems discipline
 Keep CRM records complete and current, with a scheduled next action on every open opportunity
 Log activity accurately, because your forecast and your credit both depend on it
 What We Are Looking For
 Commercial drive.  You want to carry a number and you want to beat it.
 Resilience.  High-volume outreach means high-volume rejection. You need to make the next call sound like the first one.
 Coachability.  This tier exists partly to develop you. The people who progress fastest ask for feedback and visibly act on it.
 Process discipline.  You will run recurring operational workflows (billing audits, cadence management, CRM hygiene) that protect revenue. Reliability here is the foundation of customer trust.
 Commercial instinct.  You notice when a routine support question is actually an expansion signal, and you do something about it.
 Clear written communication.  Your emails, customer-facing content, and CRM notes are all read by someone who will judge us on them.
 Customer empathy.  You will handle billing disputes and pricing conversations. Doing that well protects both the relationship and the revenue.
 Curiosity about the platform.  The Associates who become Specialists learned their platform properly, not just the pitch.
 Autonomy and Escalation
 You operate inside a structured playbook with a clear escalation path. Escalation is a strength at this tier, not a weakness.
 Decide yourself:  standard pricing and terms, routine renewals, day-to-day account management within cadence.
 Escalate: 
 Any discount request, however small
 Any at-risk account signal, immediately
 Billing discrepancies above defined thresholds
 Growth opportunities in your accounts that need a Manager or Director, routed with full context
 Requests for non-standard contract terms, service commitments, or SLAs
 Quota and Compensation
 You will carry a quarterly quota weighted heavily toward new business, with expansion and renewal making up the balance. Quota is set from your assigned accounts and territory rather than a generic benchmark, and it ramps across your first two quarters so you are not held to full target while you are still learning.
 Compensation is a competitive base plus variable, with the variable tied to new business won, pipeline quality, and team performance. We will walk you through targets, weightings, and exactly how performance is measured during the interview process.
 Where This Leads
 Associate is the first rung of a four-tier track. Typical progression to  Partnership & Growth Specialist  takes 12 to 24 months.
 To be promoted you will need to show: 
 Two consecutive quarters at or above quota
 Clean, independent ownership of your named accounts
 Ability to run discovery unsupervised
 Evidence you have informally coached at least one peer
 Compensation and logistics
 On-target earnings: $130k CAD  (base ~$50-70k plus variable). Variable is tied to closed-won new business. When our MD or CCO leads the close on an enterprise deal, you share in the win for the pipeline you built and advanced
 Full benefits
 Remote within Canada, with working hours that overlap Eastern Time, where most of our team sits. 
 Some travel expected, predominantly within North America

At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it. 



We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our Product Platform org - the group that powers product development across Vanta by building the shared foundations that every engineering team builds on top of. This hire will join one of two closely-aligned teams within the org, each working on foundational challenges with company-wide impact.

 

Application Primitives is responsible for the shared, customer-facing platform components that product teams implement across the product: examples include comments, notifications platform, event log infrastructure, and agentic audit trails. This team sits at the intersection of platform and product - not pure infrastructure, not pure product - building the reusable building blocks that let other teams ship faster and more consistently.

 

Libraries & Foundations is a brand-new team that owns Vanta's internal engineering libraries and golden-path patterns. Sitting between core platform and product platform in the stack, this team builds the TypeScript-first abstractions and shared foundations that all Vanta engineers build on top of - including event-driven architecture libraries, code quality tooling, and test frameworks.

 

You'll be evaluated for both teams based on your background and interests, and the decision on team placement will reflect where your skills and passions are the strongest fit.

 

Visit our Vanta Engineering Blog https://www.vanta.com/all-categories/engineering to learn more about what our team is working on! 

 

What you’ll do as a Senior Software Engineer, Product Platform at Vanta:

 - Design and build high-quality, scalable systems and shared libraries that multiple engineering teams depend on - whether that's shared customer-facing components (Applications Primitives) or internal abstractions (Libraries & Foundations)

 -  Partner deeply with product engineering teams to understand their needs and translate them into clean, well-documented APIs and services

 -  Drive technical decisions and influence architecture across team boundaries, with a focus on developer experience and platform scalability

 -  Define and uphold engineering standards for shared components, ensuring consistency, performance, and security across the systems you own

 -  Participate actively in code review, design discussions, and technical planning - raising the engineering quality bar for your team and beyond

 -  Write and maintain thorough documentation for the systems and libraries you build, enabling engineers across the org to use and contribute to them

 - Contribute to building Vanta's engineering culture as we scale

 

How to be successful in this role:

 - Industry experience in backend or fullstack software engineering, with a focus on platform, shared infrastructure, or developer-facing systems

 - Experience building shared APIs, services, or platform components used by multiple engineering teams - a platform mindset is critical

 - Familiarity with distributed systems, event-driven architecture, or message queue systems (Kafka, SQS, pub/sub)

 - Excellent communication skills - able to work cross-functionally with engineering, product, and design stakeholders, and to clearly articulate technical trade-offs

 - Track record of shipping high-quality, maintainable code with sound judgment on architectural decisions

 - Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.

 

What you can expect as a Vanta’n:

 - Industry-competitive salary and equity

 - 100% covered medical, dental, and vision benefits with dependents coverage

 - Pension contribution

 - 16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents

 - Health & wellness stipend

 - Remote workspace, internet, and cellphone stipend

 - Flexible work hours and location

 - 21 days of Vacation Time and 80 hours of Sick Leave

 - 11 company-paid holidays

 - Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events!

 - Offices in SF, NYC, London, Dublin, Tel Aviv, and Sydney

Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors and may vary based on candidate location, skills, depth of work experience, and relevant licenses/credentials.

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender identity, age, religion, sexual orientation, veteran or disability status, or any other protected class. As an equal opportunity employer, we encourage and welcome people of all backgrounds to apply.



About Vanta

We started in 2018, in the wake of several high-profile data breaches. Online security was only becoming more important, but we knew firsthand how hard it could be for fast-growing companies to invest the time and manpower it takes to build a solid security foundation. Vanta was inspired by a vision to restore trust in internet businesses by enabling companies to improve and prove their security. From our early days automating security monitoring for compliance standards like SOC 2, HIPAA and ISO 27001 to creating the world's leading Trust Management Platform, our vision remains unchanged. 

Now more than ever, making security continuous—not just a point-in-time check— is essential. Thousands of companies rely on Vanta to build, maintain and demonstrate their trust— all in a way that's real-time and transparent.

Automotive Service Technician – Collision & Mechanical Services
 We are seeking an experienced Automotive Service Technician (310S) or skilled automotive technician with professional shop experience to join our collision repair operation.
 We are primarily an EV-focused collision repair facility , working extensively with electric vehicles and the systems, components, and repair procedures associated with modern EV platforms. The successful candidate will receive ongoing exposure and training in EV repair and diagnostics as part of their role.
 This position offers an opportunity to play an important role in our mechanical operations, with a primary focus on mechanical inspection, diagnosis, and repair of collision-damaged vehicles .
 As part of the continued development of our business, we are also establishing a dedicated mechanical service offering from our existing collision repair facility. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to perform general mechanical repairs and service work for local customers while supporting the mechanical requirements of our collision operation.
 We are looking for an experienced, dependable technician who takes pride in their work, has strong diagnostic ability, and is interested in developing their skills in both conventional and electric vehicle repair.
 Position Responsibilities
 The primary focus of this position will be the mechanical assessment and repair of vehicles involved in collisions.
 Responsibilities will include:
 Performing mechanical inspections of collision-damaged vehicles
 Identifying steering, suspension, drivetrain, braking, cooling, HVAC, and other mechanical damage resulting from collisions
 Identifying hidden or secondary mechanical damage that may not be immediately visible
 Performing pre-repair and post-repair mechanical inspections
 Removing and replacing suspension components, control arms, knuckles, wheel bearings, steering components, subframes, and related assemblies
 Performing wheel alignments and interpreting alignment measurements
 Assisting with engine, transmission, drive-unit, and drivetrain removal when required for collision repairs
 Performing cooling system and A/C repairs related to collision damage
 Performing A/C recovery, vacuum, and recharge procedures
 Performing mechanical diagnostic scans and basic electrical diagnosis
 Inspecting wiring, connectors, sensors, harnesses, grounds, and component mounting locations for collision-related damage
 Assisting with ADAS-related mechanical preparation and calibration procedures
 Following OEM repair information and manufacturer repair procedures
 Accurately documenting inspection findings and additional damage
 Completing post-repair mechanical inspections and quality-control checks
 Road testing vehicles when appropriate
 Maintaining a clean, organized, and professional work area
 EV Training & Exposure
 As an EV-focused collision repair facility , electric vehicles are a significant part of our daily operations.
 The successful candidate will have the opportunity to develop practical knowledge and experience working with EV systems and repair procedures, including exposure to:
 EV-specific mechanical systems
 Electric drive units and related components
 High-voltage vehicle systems and safety procedures
 EV cooling and thermal management systems
 EV-specific diagnostic procedures and scan tools
 Electrical and electronic systems
 OEM EV repair procedures
 EV-specific collision damage assessment
 Pre- and post-repair scanning
 ADAS and vehicle electronics
 Previous EV experience is an asset, but it is not required. We recognize that EV technology is a developing area of the automotive industry and will provide appropriate training and hands-on exposure to help the successful candidate develop these skills.
 Mechanical Service Opportunity
 In addition to collision-related mechanical work, this position will support the development of a general mechanical service operation within our existing facility.
 The successful candidate will have the opportunity to perform local repair and maintenance work, including:
 Brake and suspension repairs
 Steering and drivability repairs
 Diagnostic services
 Wheel alignments
 Cooling system repairs
 A/C service and repair
 Electrical diagnosis
 General mechanical repairs and maintenance
 EV and hybrid service and repair as appropriate
 Other automotive repair and service work as the department develops
 Our existing collision operation provides an established customer base and facility from which to develop this additional service segment.
 The expectation is that the mechanical service offering will develop progressively, with the technician taking on an increasing role in general mechanical repair and customer work as the operation develops.
 Qualifications
 We are seeking a technician with either a 310S Automotive Service Technician licence or significant professional experience working in an automotive repair facility.
 Candidates should have:
 Strong mechanical knowledge and practical repair experience
 Diagnostic and problem-solving ability
 Experience working safely and efficiently in a professional shop environment
 The ability to inspect a vehicle and accurately determine required repairs
 Strong attention to detail
 The ability to work independently while maintaining communication with the collision repair team
 A professional approach to workmanship, documentation, and customer service
 A valid driver's licence
 Apprentices with substantial shop experience may also be considered where their practical skills and experience align with the requirements of the position.
 Additional Experience Considered an Asset
 Experience in any of the following areas would be considered an asset:
 Collision repair or collision-related mechanical inspection
 Steering and suspension diagnosis
 Wheel alignment
 Scan tools and diagnostic equipment
 Electrical diagnosis
 EV or hybrid vehicle systems
 EV high-voltage safety and service procedures
 EV diagnostic equipment
 ADAS systems and calibration
 A/C service
 Tesla or other OEM-specific training
 Engine, transmission, drivetrain, or subframe removal
 OEM repair information and service procedures
 I-CAR or other collision-industry training
 The Right Candidate
 The successful candidate will be someone who approaches automotive repair from a diagnostic and technical perspective.
 You should be comfortable determining not only what component has failed or been damaged, but why , and whether other components or systems may have been affected.
 Particular attention will be given to candidates who demonstrate:
 Strong diagnostic reasoning
 Attention to vehicle safety and repair quality
 Professional and consistent work habits

The Role
 At Treewalk, you'll run the day-to-day finance engine for the Indigenous governments, organizations and businesses we serve: clean books, a disciplined month-end close, timely funder reporting and year-end files that sail through audit. You'll own a portfolio of clients, acting as their fractional controller. Some will lean on you to keep operations running smoothly month to month; others will need you to get a backlog cleaned up and audit-ready. Either way, every file is yours to run.
 Deadlines are real; overtime isn't a lifestyle. We staff sensibly, treat extra hours as the rare exception, and back that up with true schedule autonomy and remote flexibility, so your evenings stay yours.
 If you've managed controllership or audit-prep engagements at a small- to mid-size firm, or run finance operations inside a First Nation, Tribal Council or Indigenous organization, and you're ready for high-impact work, tangible ownership and genuine balance, then we would love to hear from you.
 How You'll Create Impact Day-to-Day
 •         Run a disciplined close – Lead month-end and year-end close across your portfolio: reconciliations, accruals, deferred revenue, capital assets and journal entries, on time and review-ready.
 •         Keep operations humming – Oversee AP, AR, payroll and cash management processes, and step in hands-on when a client needs a fractional controller's precision and speed.
 •         Make audits painless – Build year-end audit files and lead schedules, prep airtight support, clear PBC lists and quarterback conversations with external auditors so leadership can sleep at night.
 •         Get the hard files back on track – Clean up backlogs and prior-year issues, so clients go from catch-up mode to a clean, audit-ready position.
 •         Run the engine of multi-entity groups – Keep the books straight across Nations' governments, economic development corporations, limited partnerships, trusts and societies, including intercompany and fund accounting.
 •         Keep funding on track – Track funding by program, manage deferred and restricted funds, and prepare reporting for ISC, CIRNAC, FNHA and other funders.
 •         Build strong controls – Design practical processes, internal controls and financial policies that hold up to auditor and funder scrutiny.
 •         Grow the team – Coach and review the work of accountants, bookkeepers and CPA students, and build checklists and templates that scale across clients.
 Result: clients see you as the calm, trusted voice who keeps their books clean, their funders satisfied and their audits uneventful, while you build deep, meaningful expertise without the grind of traditional public practice. 
 Our ideal candidate...
 •         CPA designation required.
 •         Significant experience in controllership, month-end close and year-end audit preparation, ideally with Indigenous governments, organizations or not-for-profits.
 •         Strong working knowledge of PSAS / ASNPO, fund accounting and funding agreement reporting.
 •         Experience leading engagements and supervising staff.
 •         A respectful, relationship-based approach and an understanding of Indigenous histories, governance and the impacts of colonization.
 •         After the base experience requirements are met, we hire first and foremost strong analytical thinkers and problem solvers.
 Please mention these bonus skills if you have them
 •         Audit experience at a firm serving First Nations or public-sector clients

 Why Treewalk Feels Different
 It's Treewalk for a reason: we invest in your growth, trust your judgment, and protect your life outside the ledger.

 Who We Are
 Treewalk is Vancouver-born and scaling nationwide. Our Indigenous Services group runs the finance operations of Nations and Indigenous organizations and gets them audit-ready, so leadership can focus on their community's goals while we keep the numbers strong.
 But labels like "accounting firm" don't capture our DNA. Picture a tech startup powered by CPAs:
 •         Holacracy over hierarchy – Ideas outrank titles, and ownership lives on every desk.
 •         Relationships first – We earn trust over the long term and work in a way that respects each community's priorities and protocols.
 •         Growth at warp speed – One of Canada's fastest-rising advisory practices, we set audacious goals, then sprint past them.

 The Values That Power Us

 Support: No one goes it alone; collaboration is our default setting.

 Respect and Inclusion

As a Material Handler / Inside Sales Associate, you will be responsible for managing customer orders from initial inquiry through fulfillment, while maintaining warehouse operations. You will pick, pack, and ship customer orders, count and verify incoming vendor material and customer returns, and provide exceptional customer service through sales assistance, quotations and strong customer service. Your attention to detail and customer-focused approach will ensure the highest level of customer satisfaction and support revenue growth.
 To experience success in the position, you will:
 Provide a professional and consultative atmosphere for our customers
 Uphold our core values and ethics with every interaction
 Work safely and effectively as a teammate
 Be comfortable multitasking when assisting customers, supporting sales inquiries, and managing warehouse operations
 Know how to safely operate a forklift and other material handling equipment
 Be courteous, friendly, and build lasting relationships with customers and vendors
 Develop and apply comprehensive product knowledge to support customer needs and sales opportunities
 Job Duties and Responsibilities 
 Follow all Health and Safety rules and legislation while performing job functions
 Load and unload trucks, operate forklift and other material handling equipment
 Receiving duties include: Upon unloading vendor shipments or customer returns, obtain the packing slip and verify material received. Note any discrepancies or damaged material
 Print and verify the computer receiving documents and enter material received into the computer system
 Identify special order material and damaged material and store in proper location
 Note all shipping discrepancies on freight carrier's Bill of Lading, initiate freight claims and forward paperwork to appropriate teammate
 Picking, packing, and shipping duties include: Pick material for customer orders, counting and comparing items to the shipping documentation
 Assemble material and pack appropriately for pick up or shipment to customer
 Complete documentation for any shipments being delivered via third party carrier or requiring Transportation of Dangerous Goods documentation
 Inside Sales Support responsibilities include: Assist customers at the counter by answering product inquiries, providing recommendations, and processing orders
 Support sales teammates by gathering product information, preparing quotes, and addressing customer requests about product specifications and packaging
 Identify and communicate customer needs and sales opportunities to the sales team
 Maintain product knowledge to effectively support customer inquiries and contribute to sales conversations
What we are looking for from you: 
 Grade 12 diploma or equivalent; College and/or University degree an asset
 A minimum of 1 year of warehouse experience preferred
 Outstanding customer service and verbal communication skills
 Able to develop comprehensive product knowledge
 Ability to learn to safely operate a forklift and any other material handling equipment
 Possess a high level of attention to detail
 Able to learn and operate the applicable software system used to process orders
 Intermediate math skills
 Preferred Skills 
 Previous experience with or knowledge of products sold at the Profit Centre
 Experience using M3, Word, Excel, and Outlook

Aviso : 
 À Aviso, nous nous consacrons à l’amélioration du bien-être financier des Canadiennes et des Canadiens. À titre d’organisation de gestion de patrimoine de premier plan, nous nous engageons à faire preuve de leadership, d’innovation et de responsabilité ainsi qu’à miser sur le partenariat et la communauté. En travaillant avec des professionnels talentueux et énergiques qui incarnent nos valeurs au quotidien, vous constaterez rapidement que ce sont nos employés et notre culture « uneaviso » dynamique qui nous démarquent des autres sociétés. Si vous êtes à la recherche d’un emploi intéressant et stimulant au sein d’une entreprise centrée sur son personnel, découvrez ce que Aviso peut vous offrir en consultant le site www.aviso.ca/fr .
 L’occasion: 
 Nous sommes à la recherche d’un superviseur ou d’une superviseure des transferts bilingue qui se joindra à notre équipe de l’Exploitation.
 Relevant du gestionnaire ou de la gestionnaire, Exploitation, le superviseur ou la superviseure des transferts bilingue est responsable de superviser l’équipe chargée des transferts, de gérer les volumes de travail et de veiller au respect des échéances quotidiennes. Les responsabilités de supervision comprennent le recrutement, la formation, l’encadrement, le mentorat et l’établissement des horaires du personnel, y compris la supervision de l’accueil et de l’intégration des nouveaux employés ainsi que l’évolution de carrière et les possibilités de perfectionnement professionnel.
 En tant qu’uneaviso : 
 Nous prenons soin de vous – Vous faites ce qu’il faut pour la clientèle, les partenaires et les collègues. Vous établissez des relations de confiance, prônez l’excellence du service et contribuez à une culture où chaque personne se sent valorisée et soutenue. 
 Nous osons – Vous remettez en question le statu quo au moyen d’idées audacieuses et de nouvelles perspectives. Vous accueillez le changement, recherchez des occasions d’innovation et êtes à l’aise avec l’exploration de nouvelles méthodes de travail. 
 Nous nous surpassons – Vous collaborez ouvertement et établissez des relations significatives. Vous recherchez des points de vue variés, partagez vos connaissances et travaillez de concert avec les collègues, la clientèle et les partenaires pour les aider à réussir. 
 Nous livrons des résultats – Vous assumez la responsabilité de votre travail, respectez vos engagements et vous concentrez sur la production de résultats concrets. Vous êtes responsable de vos actions et cherchez constamment à vous améliorer. 
 À quoi ressemble votre journée: 
 Fixer des normes pour les procédures du service et en effectuer le suivi, en vue d’assurer la qualité, l’exactitude et l’efficacité du travail dans le respect des contrats de niveau de service
 Créer un climat positif et empreint de leadership en gagnant le respect du personnel, des pairs et des parties intéressées
 S’assurer que les membres du personnel bénéficient d’une formation et d’un perfectionnement appropriés en temps opportun
 Encadrer le personnel en vue d’améliorer le rendement tout en augmentant/maintenant l’engagement des employés ainsi que leur avancement professionnel, et soutenir l’accueil et l’intégration des nouveaux employés
 Veiller à ce que tous les processus et toutes les procédures soient à jour dans tous les manuels – internes et externes, y compris les contrats de niveau de service du service
 Se charger des communications internes et externes en suivant les canaux de distribution appropriés, en faisant la liaison avec les fournisseurs externes et les fiduciaires, le cas échéant
 Analyser les pratiques commerciales actuelles et cerner les domaines dans lesquels le service peut améliorer ses processus, faire des recommandations et mettre en place des procédures pour rationaliser le flux de travail
 Gérer le travail lié aux projets du service et participer à la mise en œuvre d’initiatives du service et de la division, selon les besoins, et déléguer si nécessaire
 Appuyer le personnel dans le cadre de problèmes complexes ou transmis à un échelon supérieur, répondre à toutes les demandes de renseignements des clients (internes et externes) et veiller à ce que les niveaux de service à la clientèle soient maintenus au sein du service, en informant la direction, le cas échéant
 Prévoir les effectifs appropriés ainsi que les besoins de formation et de perfectionnement, y compris la formation polyvalente du personnel de sorte que les employés soient à jour et puissent s’acquitter des tâches exigées dans le cadre de chacun des postes au sein de l’équipe
 Examiner et approuver les écritures de journal quotidiennes et les rapprochements de compte mensuels (OCRCVM et ACCFM)
 Rendre compte tous les mois, en temps opportun, des normes prévues par les contrats de niveau de service, y compris les exceptions, et créer des plans d’affaires pour gérer les ressources en cas de volumes élevés
 Se tenir au courant des initiatives et des normes du secteur (ACCFM et OCRCVM) et actualiser ses connaissances sur les produits de régimes enregistrés, le service NELTC de la CDS, les règles de l’OCRCVM et de l’ACCFM, les lois et les protocoles
 Faire la liaison avec la direction en ce qui concerne les rapports sur les processus et les procédures destinés aux vérificateurs externes et internes, selon les besoins
 Requirements

 Études postsecondaires et formation continue en lien avec le secteur des placements, plus précisément les fonctions liées aux opérations 
 Connaissance approfondie des exigences réglementaires pertinentes, et CFIC ou CCVM suivi avec succès, un atout
 De trois à cinq ans d’expérience à des niveaux de responsabilité de plus en plus élevés dans le secteur des placements, dont un à deux ans dans un rôle de supervision
 Excellentes compétences en matière de délégation, d’organisation, de gestion du temps et d’administration
 Grand souci du détail et de l’exactitude
 Capacité à travailler sous pression, à établir des priorités et à respecter les contraintes de temps
 Solides compétences analytiques et en résolution de problèmes, et capacité de gérer plusieurs tâches tout en ayant le souci du détail
 Excellentes aptitudes pour le service à la clientèle et capacité à rapidement cerner et résoudre les problèmes d’une manière satisfaisante pour toutes les parties
 Grande motivation, notamment pour l’atteinte des objectifs
 Connaissances informatiques intermédiaires en MS Word, Excel, Outlook et Access. Des compétences avancées sur Excel sont un atout
 Excellentes aptitudes en communication, à la fois en français et en anglais, requises
 Benefits 
 Pourquoi Aviso Wealth ? 
 Chez Aviso Wealth, vous trouverez une culture dynamique et inclusive qui valorise l’innovation et met en valeur les réussites de ses employés.
 Quelques traits qui nous distinguent : 
 Un programme de rémunération concurrentiel qui récompense et valorise les contributions de chacun.
 Des prestations de santé, soins dentaires et une assurance de premier plan pour satisfaire les divers besoins de nos employés
 Des vacances généreuses, des bénéfices de santé et de conditionnement physique, des options complémentaires au congé parental.
 Des cotisations complémentaires pour notre programme de retraite.
 Un engagement à l’amélioration continue de notre personnel au moyen de l’apprentissage et du développement ainsi que d’un programme de soutien à la formation.
 Des événements sociaux organisés régulièrement pour favoriser le travail d’équipe.
 Vos renseignements 
 En soumettant votre candidature, vous consentez à la collecte, à l’utilisation et à la communication des renseignements personnels que vous avez fournis dans le but d’évaluer vos qualifications et votre aptitude à occuper un emploi à Aviso. Vos renseignements seront traités conformément aux lois canadiennes sur la protection des renseignements personnels applicables, notamment la Loi sur la protection des renseignements personnels et les documents électroniques (LPRPDE) et les lois provinciales pertinentes. Vos données peuvent être communiquées au personnel autorisé participant au processus de recrutement et ne seront conservées que pendant la durée nécessaire à ces fins ou conformément à la loi.
 Pour obtenir plus d’informations, consultez le lien sur la Politique de protection des renseignements personnels , qui se trouve sur notre page Carrières.
 Politique d’égalité d’accès à l’emploi 
 Aviso accueille et encourage les candidatures de toutes les personnes qualifiées, y compris les candidats/titulaires handicapés. Si vous nécessitez un accommodement, nous travaillerons avec vous pour répondre à vos besoins à toutes les étapes du processus d’embauche.
 Nous remercions tous les candidats de leur intérêt, cependant, seules les candidatures retenues pour une étude plus approfondie seront contactées.
 Aucun recruteur ou agence, s’il vous plaît.
 Aperçu de la société 
 Fort d’un actif total sous administration et sous gestion environ 145 milliards de dollars, et d’un effectif de plus de 1 000 employés, Aviso est un important fournisseur de services de gestion de patrimoine et de placement pour le secteur financier canadien. Nous bâtissons un écosystème complet de services de gestion de patrimoine à la fine pointe de la technologie et axé sur les clients. Nos clients comprennent nos partenaires, les conseillers et les investisseurs. Nous sommes un partenaire de confiance pour presque toutes les coopératives d’épargne et de crédit au Canada, en plus de l’être pour un large éventail de gestionnaires de portefeuille, de courtiers en placement, de compagnies d’assurance, de sociétés de fiducie et de courtiers remisiers. Nos partenaires comptent sur Aviso pour leur offrir des solutions bien précises qui leur procurent un avantage concurrentiel dans un secteur en pleine évolution et hautement compétitif. Notre courtier en placement, notre courtier en épargne collective et nos services d’assurance soutiennent des milliers de conseillers en placement. Notre gestionnaire d’actifs est Placements NEI, dont la spécialisation est d’investir de façon responsable. Notre service de courtage en ligne, Qtrade Investissement directMD, renforce le pouvoir des investisseurs autonomes, et notre service de placement entièrement automatisé, Portefeuilles accompagnés QtradeMD, est au service des investisseurs qui préfèrent une approche passive. Partenaires des correspondants Aviso offre des services de garde de biens et de courtier chargé de compte à un large éventail de sociétés. Nous avons des bureaux à Toronto, Vancouver, Montréal et Winnipeg. Aviso est soutenue par la force collective de ses propriétaires : les centrales de caisses de crédit, Co-operators/CUMIS et Desjardins. Nous sommes fiers de propulser les entreprises qui renforcent le pouvoir des investisseurs. 
 Faire carrière à Aviso, c’est faire partie d’un groupe de professionnels talentueux et énergiques qui vivent leurs valeurs au quotidien, et appartenir à une organisation qui se consacre à votre réussite et au développement de votre carrière. Si vous êtes à la recherche d’un travail intéressant et stimulant au sein d’une société soucieuse de son personnel, postulez pour faire partie de notre équipe!
 Salaire 
 L’échelle salariale prévue de ce poste est de 83 000 $ à 100 000 $ CA par année. Les conditions de rémunération individuelles sont basées sur divers facteurs propres à chaque candidat et aux exigences du poste.

Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.
 We are looking for a Director of Supply Chain Management to build and lead the operating infrastructure required to bring our products to market, scale them globally, and support them throughout their lifecycle. This role sits within the Supply Chain organization and reports to the Sr. Director, Operations & Strategic Partnerships. This role has high exposure to CEO level decisions and engagement and demonstrated leadership experience is a requirement.
 This is a builder role within the Supply Chain. You will own the Supply Chain deliverables covering our cross functional go to market and customer engagement. This includes driving product certifications and market readiness, enhancing RMA and customer satisfaction processes, as well as driving our Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. Your job is to establish clear ownership, build scalable processes, develop the team, and create the operating mechanisms required to support a rapidly growing hardware business, working in close partnership with the other functions needed to achieve these goals.
 We are not looking for someone to administer existing processes. We are looking for someone who sees ambiguity, creates structure, drives decisions, and most importantly takes end-to-end ownership. Your mandate is simple: build it, own it, and scale it.
 This role is hybrid, based out of Toronto, ON; Austin, TX; or Santa Clara, CA. 
 We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.
 Who You Are 
 A builder who is comfortable entering an environment where processes and ownership are not fully defined, then turning ambiguity into a clear operating model and an executable plan.
 An experienced hardware and supply chain operator who understands how Engineering, Product, Sales, Manufacturing, Quality, Finance, Legal, and customer teams connect across the product lifecycle.
 A cross-functional leader who can align senior stakeholders, establish decision rights, and drive accountability without waiting for someone else to define ownership.
 A data-driven and analytically rigorous decision-maker who can make sound judgments with incomplete information and maintain urgency through execution.
 A people leader who develops strong teams, builds subject matter expertise, and creates a culture of ownership, transparency, and continuous improvement.
 What We Need 
 Drive cross-functional processes and own Supply Chain deliverables for global product certification and market readiness, including certification roadmaps across products and countries, clear readiness gates, coordination with Engineering, Product, Legal, manufacturing partners, test labs, and regulatory bodies, and early mitigation of risks that could affect customer commitments or launches.
 Own and mature the company’s S&OP process by connecting customer demand, Sales forecasts, supply, manufacturing capacity, inventory, and financial objectives into a disciplined operating cadence and trusted view for executive decision-making.
 Build and own the end-to-end global RMA and customer operations model within Supply Chain, covering intake, triage, replacement, repair, warranty management, disposition, customer communication, service levels, escalation paths, and performance metrics, in partnership with Customer, Quality, and Engineering teams.
 Establish the processes, systems, KPIs, dashboards, governance, and operating mechanisms required to scale, including measures for forecast accuracy, supply performance, inventory health, backlog, certification readiness, RMA performance, and execution against plan.
 Lead cross-functional execution with Sales, Product, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Manufacturing, test labs, regulatory bodies, and customer teams. Establish clear decision rights, simplify complex workflows, identify gaps before they become business problems, and drive shared decisions through to completion while retaining Supply Chain ownership of the deliverables.
 What You Will Learn 
 Gain broad exposure to the full operating model of a rapidly growing hardware and semiconductor business, from product development and global market readiness through supply planning, manufacturing, delivery, and customer support.
 Build expertise in integrating Supply Chain-owned certification deliverables, S&OP, RMA, and customer operations into one scalable product lifecycle operating system.
 Develop the leadership and operating mechanisms required to turn cross-functional complexity into clear ownership, timely decisions, and measurable execution.
 See directly how operational decisions influence product launch timing, customer commitments, product quality, inventory, revenue, and the company’s ability to scale globally.
 Create the foundation for a supply chain management organization that grows with Tenstorrent’s products, markets, customers, and operational complexity.

Functionally reports to Extrusion Team Lead. Responsible for optimally operating the press, process equipment, handling equipment and die setup in a safe and efficient manner. Responsible for following Company policies and procedures by ensuring a safe working environment is maintained at all times.  We believe that every Employee is responsible to act safely and to model good safety practices.
 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 The duties and responsibilities of the Press Operator are detailed below, but not limited to the following:
 Efficiently operate the extrusion press while maintaining good quality that meets Almag’s quality standards. 
 Keep track of equipment performance and ensure press is well tuned, and temperatures are being properly managed from billet oven to press exit temperatures.
 Responsible for monitoring runout efficiency such as length, speed, and finish.
 Reference work orders to ensure press is running at the optimal speeds to maximize productivity.
 Ensure billet zone temperatures are setup, monitored and maintained throughout the runs. Mark extrusions accordingly if temperatures do not meet requirements.
 Die management - Ensure all necessary tooling is available at the beginning and throughout shift.
 Load dies into press and ensure presses are not waiting for die changes. Importance must be given to ensure dies are not loaded too early or too late.
 Ensure die temperatures are maintained when dies are loaded and removed from the ovens.
 Responsible for communicating directly with the team leads/maintenance team if any mechanical breakdowns or issues are encountered.
 Ensure proper billets/logs are in the ovens and monitor the supply to keep press going.
 Ensure average speeds are followed based on information contained on work orders. If deviations occur, ensure note is made in EPICS and Team Lead is notified.
 Responsible for EPICS entries for billet lengths, cut offs, cut sizes, etc., and highlight any special notes and instructions that the team needs to focus on. 
 Responsible for entering all downtime, die fails, quality issues, and schedule adherence notes in EPICS.
 Responsible for checking notes in EPICS and viewing drawings throughout the shift to ensure work orders are followed correctly.
 Responsible for checking the run out on the second billet produced. Report to Team Lead if billet length scheduled is inappropriate and have it changed to improve yield.
 Ensure sufficient spacing is kept between extrusion pieces on the cooling table to make sure proper cooling is maintained.
 Responsible for ensuring the extrusion is correctly fed into puller jaws. Notify maintenance/team lead if any issues occur.
 Ensure exit/runout temperatures are monitored and maintained throughout the run. 
 Maintain quality checks at front end of press during operation and continuously throughout the shift.
 Press samples must be properly labelled and kept together for traceability
 Ensure samples are taken after the first billet and verify dimensions and surface finish according to drawings in EPICS.
 Ensure all billets and alloys used are accounted for in EPICS and documented accurately.
 Check finish and dimensions on extrusions at the required frequency.
 Complete press Ascona scans as required.
 Must have knowledge and ability to operate all equipment at saw and stretcher.
 Other duties as assigned. 
 MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS 
 Education/Experience 
 High school Diploma with some technical background and mechanical aptitude.
 Extrusion experience is an asset.
 Technical Skills/Competence 
 1-2 years’ experience in an industrial environment.
 Knowledge of machinery and ability to read drawings is an asset. Willing to train.  
 Must be willing and able to train and develop as a saw operator / inspector, stretcher operator and die preparation operator as understating these jobs and their impact is critical to developing as a competent press operator.
 Basic computer skills including MS Windows is required. Other MS software is an asset. 
 Understanding of measurements, tolerances, basic geometry, and numeracy comprehension.
 Ability to lift up-to 50lbs independently, and ability to lift up-to 100lbs in collaboration with a team member.
 Familiarity with extrusion software such as EPICS is an asset.
