veritree and Job Overview
 veritree is an award-winning climate tech start-up based in Vancouver. Launched in 2021, our technology measures and verifies the impact of global restoration efforts from the ground up. We are on a mission to plant 1 billion verified trees by 2030, collaborating with businesses, planting organizations, and consumers who believe in the transformative power of verified restoration projects to create real and meaningful impact for the planet, nature, and people.
 veritree is seeking an Product Marketing Manager to own the commercialization of our restoration portfolio: turning every project we plant into a sales-ready package, and acting as the technical and impact expert our revenue teams bring into the room.
 We have active restoration projects across the globe, each one carries real depth, identifying the purpose behind the site, whether the trees are permanent or on a managed harvest rotation, the species mix and why it was chosen, survivability and monitoring data, the workers and communities involved, and the ecosystem returning around it. We need someone who can translate project details into one canonical source of truth, packaging it into narratives, value propositions, and assets our Sales, Business Development, and Customer Success teams can actually use, and then standing behind it on live calls.
 This role is a deliberate blend of product marketing, product ownership, and sales enablement. You will own the story of what we sell, not the marketing gloss, but the substantive, verifiable, layered version that wins enterprise deals. This is a storyteller's role first. You will be fluent enough in forestry, permanence, survivability, and our on-site technology to hold your own with a sustainability lead or a diligence team, but the reason we're hiring is narrative craft: the ability to make a Fortune 500 buyer feel what changes for a worker who once felled trees for income and now earns more, more securely, planting them.
 12 Month Key Outcomes (12m KOs)
 Source of truth, live and trusted. One canonical project library covering 100% of active projects — purpose, permanence and harvest model, species mix, survivability, monitoring methodology, workforce and community context, ecosystem outcomes — current, maintained on an agreed cadence with Forest, and surfaced in internal materials for live call support.
 Every project sales-ready. A sales-ready package shipped for every active project: positioning, value proposition, proof points, pricing guidance, and customer-facing assets. No rep builds their own version from scratch.
 Impact story, three layers deep. A worker, community, and ecosystem narrative built and evidenced for our priority projects, backed by real data and media from veritree's technology — credible enough to survive diligence, specific enough to be memorable, and never greenwashing.
 Enablement that changes rep behaviour. Playbooks, proof-point libraries, objection handling, and training delivered so every Account Executive, Business Development Rep, and Customer Success Manager tells the same story, with adoption measured through call reviews and certification rather than assumed.
 Launch discipline. A cross-functional launch checklist and readiness standard, owned by you and adopted across Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success, so nothing goes to market half-built.
 What You'll Do
 Source of Truth & Project Intelligence 
 You will build and own veritree's canonical library of project facts — one current, authoritative reference for every project we sell, replacing the scattered documents and tribal knowledge in use today.
 You will work directly with the Forest team to turn their intake into commercially usable intelligence: project purpose, permanence versus managed harvest and rotation length, species selection and rationale, survivability and mortality data, monitoring methodology, and site-level context.
 You will keep it current, with a defined maintenance cadence, clear ownership of each input, and version control the rest of the business can rely on.
 You will make it accessible where our teams actually work, surfacing project facts in Forge and our AI tooling so a rep can get an accurate answer during a live call, not after it.
 Packaging, Positioning & Pricing 
 You will translate every project into a sales-ready package: the narrative, the value proposition, the proof points, and the per-project assets that make it sellable.
 You will standardize delivery into ecosystem packages — mangrove, terrestrial, wildfire, agroforestry — rather than rebuild bespoke every deal, and you will own the product catalogue.
 You will own positioning across our growing solution portfolio, so that as we move from selling a single product toward solution-selling across multiple offerings and stakeholders, the story stays coherent.
 You will partner with Revenue and Finance on per-project pricing guidance and the commercial logic behind it, ensuring reps understand not just the price but why the project is worth it.
 You will own the change-flow when a metric is updated. When survivability, planting hours, or carbon updates, you push the correction into collateral, the portal, and CS on a set cadence — and you audit what's already in market.
 You will define which projects we lead with for which segments, and build the matching logic that helps reps put the right project in front of the right buyer.
 Impact Storytelling 
 You will build the impact narrative at three layers, and go deeper than the category norm on each:
 The worker — what this work actually changes for the individual, including the person who once cut and sold timber to feed their family and now earns better, more secure income restoring the same landscape.
 The community — how stable, better-paying restoration work compounds into local economic resilience, and what that looks like in the specific communities we operate in.
 The ecosystem — what returns to the site: canopy, soil, water, birds, wildlife, biodiversity — and how our technology measures and verifies it.
 You will ground every layer in evidence, using veritree's existing monitoring technology, field data, and media to turn claims into proof our clients can publish and defend.
 You will partner with Marketing to convert that depth into case studies, impact reports, campaign material, and event content.
 Sales Enablement 
 You will turn Forest's methodologies into sales-ready material — survivability, planting hours, social impact, carbon, permanence, verification — as defensible talk tracks, proof points, and objection handling. You know the difference between a compelling claim and a defensible one, and you only ever ship the defensible one.
 You will own the enablement library for project and impact content: playbooks, proof points, objection handling, discovery guidance, and competitive framing.
 You will design and deliver training and certification so every rep across Business Development, Sales, and Customer Success can tell the story consistently and credibly.
 You will review calls, identify where the story is breaking down, and close the gap with better material and better coaching rather than more documents.
 You will run a feedback loop from the field back into packaging, so what we ship next reflects what actually lands with buyers.
 Expert Support on Live Calls 
 You will act as the on-call project and impact expert, joining sales and Customer Success calls to explain projects in depth to prospects and customers when a rep needs the specialist in the room.
 You will handle the questions reps can't: permanence and additionality, survivability and replanting, harvest rotation and end use, monitoring and verification methodology, species and site selection, social impact measurement.
 You will represent veritree credibly in front of sustainability, ESG, and procurement stakeholders, and support diligence when deals require it.
 You will treat every call as a diagnostic. The goal is not to be permanently required on calls — it is to notice what reps couldn't answer and turn that into material and coaching so they can next time.
 You will not own the deal, carry a quota, or run the commercial conversation. The rep owns the deal; you make the rep formidable.
 Project & Product Launch 
 You will own the launch checklist and cross-functional readiness for new projects and new solutions — the definition of "ready to sell" and the gate that enforces it.
 You will own each project's availability, not just its launch — taking it online when it's ready and offline when it's sold out or paused.
 You will coordinate Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success through launch, so readiness is planned rather than scrambled.
 You will own the internal communication of what's new: what changed, what it means commercially, and what each team needs to do about it.
 Cross-Functional Partnership 
 You will sit at the seam between Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, Business Development, and Customer Success, and you will be the person all of them come to for the truth about a project.
 You will feed field and buyer insight back to Forest and Product, influencing which projects we source, how we describe them, and what our technology needs to capture next.
 Requirements 
 Professional Requirements
 Exceptional storytelling and writing ability. This is the core of the role. You can hold a room, and you can put the same idea on a page without it going flat. We will ask for writing samples and we will read them closely.
 5-8+ years in product marketing, brand or content strategy, communications, or a comparable narrative-led role. Adjacent backgrounds are welcome — journalism, documentary, impact communications, science communication — if you can show the commercial application.
 A track record of packaging complex or technical subject matter into positioning, narratives, and assets that a sales team actually adopted — with evidence of adoption, not just delivery.
 Demonstrated sales enablement experience — building playbooks, proof-point libraries, and training programs, and measuring whether they changed rep behaviour.
 Comfort being customer-facing as the subject-matter expert: you can present with authority to an enterprise audience and hold up under informed questioning, without needing to run the commercial conversation.
 Genuine appetite for technical and scientific subject matter, and the discipline to represent it accurately. You know the difference between a compelling claim and a defensible one. You do not need a forestry background — you need to be the kind of person who will go and learn it properly.
 Experience owning cross-functional process — launch checklists, readiness gates, intake-to-market workflows — in an environment where that process didn't exist yet.
 Fluency with CRM and enablement tooling (HubSpot preferred) and a builder's instinct for using AI to make knowledge accessible at the point of need.
 Based in or able to work core hours in the PST time zone, and willing to travel to customer sites, planting sites, and the Vancouver office as required.
 Personal Strengths
 A storyteller by instinct — you notice the specific detail that makes an abstract claim land, and you reach for it before the statistic.
 A builder who is comfortable creating structure, systems, and process where none exists.
 Genuinely curious about the substance — the forestry, the science, the communities — not just the pitch.
 Mission-driven, with real conviction about restoration done credibly and a low tolerance for greenwashing.
 Rigorous and detail-oriented, with the judgment to know which details matter to a buyer and which don't.
 Influences without authority: you can get Forest, Product, Marketing, and Sales moving in the same direction without owning any of them.
 Clear, direct, and calm under pressure — tech-forward and credible, never cliché.
 Nice to Haves (not mandatory)
 Experience in tree planting, forestry, carbon markets, sustainability, or nature-based solutions.
 Familiarity with ESG and nature reporting frameworks (CSRD, TNFD, SBTi, CDP).
 Experience with MRV (measurement, reporting, and verification) methodologies, remote sensing, or field data collection technology.
 Background in social impact measurement or community development.
 Experience building AI-assisted knowledge bases or enablement tooling for live call support.
 Benefits 
 Why This Role
 You will own the story of what veritree actually sells — and at a company whose entire premise is verified impact, that story is the product. It is a rare brief: real material to work with, twenty-plus projects and the people and ecosystems inside them, plus the data to prove every word of it. You will have the autonomy to build a function that doesn't exist yet, the access to go deep on projects most people only ever see as a line item, and the mandate to make sure the way we sell restoration is as rigorous as the way we deliver it.
 Benefits & Compensation Overview
 At veritree, we recognize that compensation and performance development are key to attracting and retaining top talent. Our approach is grounded in fairness, transparency, and creating opportunities for growth as both our people and business scale.
 Some highlights you can expect include:
 Competitive salary with a performance-driven framework that ensures fair and consistent compensation reviews, tied to individual impact and business growth.
 Extended health, dental, and vision benefits.
 Additional Health Spending Account (HSA) / Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA) to support your well-being and lifestyle interests.
 A variety of time-off programs, including vacation, personal days, and a 4-week remote work program each year.
 Employee discount with tentree, our sister company.
 A flexible, hybrid work environment designed for collaboration and focus-driven impact.
 veritree ensures that compensation is reviewed fairly and consistently, with opportunities for salary progression tied to sustained performance. As such, the salary range for this role including variable compensation is $93,544 to $108,186 CAD.
 This range is positioned around the 50th-75th percentile of market data we've collected, reflecting our commitment to competitive pay. Final offer amounts are based on the individual experience and skillset of the candidate demonstrated during the recruitment process.
 We reserve the >75th percentile of our salary ranges for internal employees who demonstrate sustained high performance and impact at veritree.
 veritree is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that represents diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business needs.

 Talent Pipeline Posting Notice 
Please note that this posting is not tied to an immediate vacancy. We are proactively building a pipeline of qualified candidates in anticipation of potential hiring needs over the coming months. Applications will be reviewed and retained for future consideration as opportunities arise.
 We are seeking a Lighting Artist to create high-quality real-time lighting and help support the execution of lighting work across GameSim projects.
 This is a hands-on production role with opportunities to take on project-level leadership responsibilities. In addition to completing assigned lighting work, you may help coordinate tasks, review the work of other artists, provide constructive feedback, and ensure scenes meet the visual and technical quality bar established by Art Direction and the client.
 You will collaborate with Art Directors, Environment Artists, Technical Artists, VFX Artists, Designers, Engineers, Producers, clients, and partner studios to translate creative direction into lighting solutions that support mood, gameplay readability, environmental storytelling, and performance.
 What Success Looks Like
 Within your first 90 days, you will:
 Develop a clear understanding of the project’s visual direction, lighting pipeline, gameplay requirements, technical constraints, and production schedule.
 Build effective working relationships with Art Direction, Production, Technical Art, Environment Art, Design, and other project disciplines.
 Create polished lighting work that meets the project’s established visual and technical quality bar.
 Take ownership of lighting for assigned scenes, environments, sequences, or gameplay areas.
 Provide useful feedback and support to other artists when asked to review or coordinate lighting work.
 Identify artistic, technical, or production risks early and communicate them to the appropriate project leads.
 Deliver assigned work on schedule and respond effectively to internal and client feedback.
 Responsibilities
 Lighting Creation and Execution
 Create high-quality real-time lighting for gameplay environments, levels, cinematics, characters, and interactive sequences.
 Translate art direction, concept art, reference material, gameplay requirements, narrative goals, and client feedback into effective lighting solutions.
 Use lighting to establish mood, atmosphere, visual hierarchy, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Ensure lighting supports gameplay readability, navigation, combat visibility, character presentation, and important interactive elements.
 Develop and refine exposure, color, contrast, fog, atmosphere, reflections, shadows, emissive response, color grading, and post-processing.
 Create lighting for a range of visual styles, including realistic, stylized, cinematic, and highly art-directed projects.

 Ensure completed work meets project requirements for quality, performance, organization, and delivery.
 Leadership and Quality Support

 Review the work of other lighting artists or multidisciplinary artists contributing to lighting.
 Provide clear, respectful, and actionable feedback through written notes, live reviews, reference images, paintovers, or in-engine examples.
 Help ensure lighting work follows approved visual targets, technical standards, and project requirements.
 Communicate expected outcomes, priorities, and quality standards to artists working within an assigned area.
 Monitor the visual progress of assigned lighting work and identify scenes that may require additional revision or support.
 Confirm that feedback has been addressed before work is submitted for senior, Art Director, or client review.
 Support junior or less-experienced artists with lighting fundamentals, engine workflows, scene organization, optimization, and production practices.

 Planning and Production Support

Workers' Compensation Coordinator  
 Employees can be absent from work for a variety of reasons: casual absence, work-related  illness and/or injury, or health issues requiring the employee to be away from the work place  for an extended period. Our absence management program helps employers strategically  manage those absences- focusing on reducing overall costs, realizing administrative efficiency,  and enhancing support for employees. All with the goal of returning employees to health and  productivity.   
 Our Absence Management Solutions team helps TELUS employees return to health and productivity after work-related injury, illness, or personal challenges. Your role supports this mission by ensuring every claim is processed accurately and compassionately, removing friction so our case managers can focus on the human side of recovery. 
 Responsibilities:  
 Serve as the operational backbone of the absence management team, managing the end-to-end coordination of workers' compensation claims. 
 Partner with Claims Management Coordinators and Case Managers to coordinate the flow of information, managing touchpoints with provincial workers' compensation boards and clients to ensure seamless claim processing. 
 Operating the internal system system to attach incoming documents to claims;  
 Processing invoices within our internal system Case Management Systems;  
 Communicating with the provincial boards to obtain information on claim files;  
 Communicating with clients for telephonic claim intake;   
 Opening, sorting, scanning, and storing the mail we receive;   
 Monitor key performance metrics (e.g., claim processing turnaround time) to ensure we meet service level agreements with clients and provincial boards.  
 Your attention to detail and communication keep claims on track, supporting faster claim resolution and better outcomes for injured/ill employees. 
 Succeeding as a Workers' Compensation Coordinator will require the following core  qualifications and skills (at minimum):   
 Must-have : Paralegal license with Law Society of Ontario in good standing 
 Strong to-have (not deal-breaker): Post-secondary education in health management, absence/disability management, or related field. 
 Nice-to-have: Academic coursework in health & safety, workers' comp, medical terminology, disability management, insurance, or RTW/Rehabilitation 
 Strong interpersonal skills — you communicate clearly with provincial boards, manage client intake calls professionally, and coordinate seamlessly with case managers and team members. 
 Work experience in a front-line customer support role or claims processing environment, with demonstrated commitment to strong client service.

 Opportunity to give back to communities in which we work, live and serve 
 Career growth and learning & development opportunities to develop your skills

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


WHY THIS ROLE?

This role is for a highly experienced Back-End Software Engineer who wants to work on core systems that shape how the platform (Model Vault) operates. You will help define the architecture of the platform where reliability, security, performance, and simplicity all matter, and where many of the problems do not have off-the-shelf solutions.

Model Vault is Cohere’s inference platform for deploying and operating models securely at enterprise scale. The team owns the systems between a customer and the underlying AI infrastructure, including identity, deployments, metering, billing, security, privacy, and confidential computing. We are strengthening these systems as Model Vault grows, with the goal of scaling to millions of users and supporting some of the world’s most demanding enterprise workloads.



AS A SENIOR/STAFF SOFTWARE ENGINEER, YOU WILL:

 - Evolve and scale the backend systems that power Model Vault, including authentication and authorization, deployment management, billing, metering, and customer lifecycle.

 - Lead major architectural initiatives across identity, payments, usage systems, platform scalability, and other core product foundations.

 - Build highly reliable control-plane services for provisioning, configuring, scaling, and operating model deployments across clouds and hardware platforms.

 - Design APIs and distributed systems with strong guarantees around correctness, consistency, isolation, failure recovery, idempotency, and observability.

 - Build security and privacy into the platform architecture, including tenant isolation, least-privilege access, auditability, secrets management, encryption, and confidential computing boundaries.

 - Solve complex problems that span backend systems, cloud infrastructure, security, and AI inference, where conventional SaaS patterns are often not enough.

 - Drive projects end-to-end, from architecture and threat modeling through implementation, rollout, production operations, and iteration based on real customer workloads.


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF:

 - You are a strong backend engineer with excellent fundamentals in distributed systems, databases, networking, operating systems, and security.

 - You have strong programming fundamentals and experience building production systems in languages such as Go, Python, Java, C++, Rust, or similar. You write clean, maintainable, well-tested code and make thoughtful tradeoffs between simplicity, performance, and correctness.

 - You have designed and operated production systems where correctness, availability, security, and performance mattered at significant scale.

 - You can take ambiguous, high-impact technical problems, define the right architecture, and drive them through to reliable production systems.

 - You have strong systems-design instincts and understand concepts such as concurrency, consistency, caching, queues, rate limiting, backpressure, failure domains, idempotency, and graceful degradation.

 - You think deeply about security boundaries and understand authentication, authorization, identity, cryptography, secrets, tenant isolation, and how small implementation choices can create significant security risks.

 - You are comfortable reasoning across backend services, APIs, databases, distributed systems, and the cloud infrastructure they run on.

 - You are comfortable diving into unfamiliar codebases and debugging complex problems that cross service or system boundaries.

 - You care about the details of production engineering, including instrumentation, capacity planning, migrations, backwards compatibility, incident response, and safe rollouts.

 - You are comfortable challenging existing architecture and evolving foundational components when the system’s needs change.

 - You have a track record of taking technically difficult projects from an unclear starting point to systems that other engineers and customers depend on.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.



We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.



Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

Job Description 
 What is the opportunity? 
 As a key and integral member of the People Risk Governance & Oversight team, the Senior Director, People Risk Governance, Policy & Practice Lead will support the VP, People Risk Oversight & Governance in the strategy, development and execution of a centralized, enterprise-wide, 2nd line of defense Centre of Governance (CoG) practice for the People Risk domain.
 Specifically, the Senior Director will play an active and leading role in the following:
 Developing, implementing, and maintaining a clear, well-defined, framework, target operating model and strategy for global oversight of People Risk, in alignment with regulatory requirements and Enterprise risk frameworks.
 Establishing consistent risk oversight governance processes, which encompass risk identification, assessment, mitigation, reporting, and monitoring activities for the People Risk domain globally.
 Ensuring that the enterprise People Risk profile demonstrates a fair and accurate representation of risk exposure and aligns with RBC’s risk appetite.
 Providing independent and objective risk management insights, trends, analysis, and perspectives on emerging risks to enable well-informed senior leadership level discussions and action-oriented decision-making.
 Being the key lead with respect to People Risk matters globally, building processes to provide advisory support and guidance to 1LOD and 2LOD partners on People Risk escalations.
 Fostering and maintaining strong strategic relationships with internal partners across HR, Group Risk Management (GRM), Compliance, Business Segments and Functions, while championing a strong risk management mindset and culture.
 What will you do? 
 People Risk Centre of Governance : Shape and drive the global operating model and strategy for RBC’s enterprise-scope 2LOD People Risk CoG, ensuring that 1LOD and 2LOD roles and responsibilities are clearly delineated and understood by all impacted parties.  Act as key contact and subject matter expert for all People Risk management matters, fostering strong partner relationships to enable active collaboration and global consistency in the adoption and application of related risk management practices.
 Risk Governance : Owner of the People Risk framework, taxonomy, methodology and requirements, ensuring they are well-defined and align with Operational Risk and Regulatory Compliance risk management practices. Champion and lead for integrating and ensuring adherence of the universal risk practices described by the Operational Risk Management Framework. Key participant in various operational risk governance and leadership forums. Collaborate with GRM Operational Risk Management and Compliance to support convergence activities in support of risk management practices or any other enterprise methodology changes to be implemented.
 Policy Governance : Develop an enterprise-scope People Risk Policy and related standards that govern how People Risk is managed globally, while ensuring the policy remains consistent with changing industry best practices and regulatory expectations. Own and maintain all applicable 2LOD People Risk policies/standards and establish a policy architecture governance model in alignment with Enterprise Risk policy requirements. Implement policy adherence monitoring for 2LOD People Risk policies/standards, confirming whether 1LOD teams are complying with governing regulations and internal policy requirements.
 Risk Oversight, Challenge & Assessment : Provide independent oversight of the 1st LOD risk-taking and control activities and challenge risk assessments and risk decisions made through review of Risk Registers, Control Registers, Risk & Control Self-Assessments (RCSAs), Issues Management, Internal and External events, Scenario Analysis and Change Management initiatives. Advise on the alignment of the business risk appetite with the enterprise.  Monitor and challenge risk exposure and control effectiveness. Conduct and lead thematic reviews specific to identified People Risks and supporting practices.   Engage with partners across the enterprise to effectively raise issues identified through 2LOD oversight and monitoring activities.
 Regulatory & Audit Relations : Lead the review and coordination of responses of People Risk related regulatory examinations, regulator inquiries/requests for information, consultations and audit requests.
 Advisory & Training: Provide risk insight and guidance to 1st line partners on the identification of inherent People Risks and the assessment of existing controls to mitigate potential risks and reduce residual risk. Develop People risk training that provides information and education specific to People Risk and associated controls to help strengthen awareness and risk culture
 People Leadership: Manage a team of risk management professionals, providing ongoing support and coaching in furtherance of career growth and development.    
 What do you need to succeed? 
 Must Have 
 Subject-matter expertise and knowledge of operational risk and enterprise risk frameworks, with a minimum of 10 years prior work experience in risk management, an oversight function and/or regulatory compliance with a governance focus.
 Experience in driving complex, transformational initiatives at scale while providing strategic impact.
 Ability to navigate through ambiguity, bringing perspective and sound judgement to decision-making.
 Ability to influence senior leadership decision-making with precision and clarity on complex risk/regulatory matters.
 Policy management and policy governance experience.
 People leadership experience.
 Nice to Have: 
 HR, People Risk and/or employment law related experience
 Prior experience with working within a global, enterprise-wide mandate
 Strong use of Excel and PowerPoint applications
 Dashboard/reporting capabilities

ABOUT NEW ENERGY NEXUS
 New Energy Nexus (NEX) is an international NGO that supports climate solutions and builds a more equitable clean energy economy. Our laser focus is on clean energy entrepreneurs: providing them with funds, accelerators, and networks to thrive. They are our main audience and our agent of change.
We started in California in 2004 and now operate across China, India, Southeast Asia, East and West Africa, and Australia. We have leveraged US$5.4 billion in investment and supported more than 11,000 entrepreneurs.
 ABOUT THE ROLE & OPPORTUNITY
 The Director of Development Strategy & Operations will lead the internal engine behind New Energy Nexus' global fundraising and business development efforts. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this role sits at the center of NEX's development team — turning what our development and partnerships staff and country teams learn on the ground with funders into a coherent, prioritized fundraising strategy, and making sure the team is coordinated, resourced, and focused on the highest-value opportunities. 
 This is not primarily a donor-facing relationship management role. It is a strategy, team leadership, and fundraising operations role for someone who understands the business and fund development cycle deeply enough to translate frontline intelligence — what funders are signaling, what's landing and what isn't, where proposals are stalling, which markets and programs are attracting interest — into clear direction for where the team should spend its time.
 The Director will lead and develop NEX's global platform-level development team, ensuring that individual team members' skills and expertise are deployed effectively against organizational priorities, while bringing together the knowledge and fundraising capabilities of country leaders, chapter teams, and program leads. The ideal candidate has the analytical rigor and systems mindset of a strong operations leader, paired with real fluency in philanthropic and development finance fundraising, so they can be a credible internal leader and partner to a globally distributed team of fundraisers, country directors, and program leads.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 Fundraising Strategy & Prioritization (50%) 
 Help develop a living, prioritized development strategy based on proposal outcomes, funder conversations, and market signals gleaned from team conversations and learnings from fundraisers, country directors, and program leads
 Synthesize funder conversations, proposal outcomes, market signals and intelligence generated across the organization into clear fundraising priorities
 Identify where NEX should be focusing time and effort across programs and geographies, based on funder appetite, pipeline strength, and organizational priorities.
 Maintain a clear view of the funding pipeline across the network — by funder, program, chapter, and stage — and flag risks, gaps, or unrestricted-vs-restricted balance issues early.
 Translate strategy into concrete guidance: which opportunities to prioritize, which proposals need repositioning, where the team is over- or under-invested.
 Serve as a thought partner to the CEO and program leads on funding strategy, drawing on patterns across markets rather than any single relationship.
 Team Coordination & Enablement (35%) 
 Lead and develop the global platform-level development team including recruiting, hiring, onboarding, coaching, and managing performance, and ensure team members' skills are effectively leveraged against NEX's development priorities.
 Translate the development strategy into a clear rolling work plan for the team, aligning ownership, resources, and timelines.
 Build strong collaboration across the global development function, bringing together the expertise and fundraising capabilities of platform-level staff, country leaders, fundraisers, and program leads to maximize collective impact.
 Run the operating rhythm of the fundraising team: pipeline reviews, proposal coordination across programs/chapters/finance/communications, and prioritization check-ins.
 Coordinate multi-country and multi-program proposals, including combining country and program inputs into a cohesive narrative and budget that aligns with broader NEX operational and growth priorities.
 Build and own a central library of fundraising collateral - pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, program summaries, impact data - so materials for funder meetings and conference talks can be assembled quickly rather than built from scratch each time.
 Draft and maintain core funder and conference decks, adapting a standard set of modular slides/content to each audience so our fundraisers can focus their time on external relationship-building and speaking rather than deck production.
 Partner with the Chief Communications Officer to keep collateral aligned with current messaging, program updates, and brand standards.
 Provide country leads and fundraisers with the tools, templates, frameworks, and support to raise funds effectively and report consistently.
 Build feedback loops so that what is learned through funder and country-level engagement consistently makes its way back into strategy, priorities, and team planning.
 Systems, Data & Reporting (15%) 
 Accountable for the fundraising CRM and pipeline-tracking systems, ensuring data quality, consistent use across chapters, and useful reporting.
 Produce regular and ad hoc reporting and dashboards for NEX leadership on pipeline health, funder trends, and progress against platform fundraising goals.
 Standardize proposal, reporting, and stewardship templates and processes across the global platform-level team.
 Track outcomes against the fundraising strategy and refine it as new data comes in.
 Ensure fundraising protocols and internal as well as external reporting are completed on time and to consistent quality standards
 SUCCESS IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS
 Success in this role will mean building a more coordinated, strategic, and effective global development function. By the end of the first 6–12 months, the Director will have:
 Established clear visibility into NEX's global fundraising pipeline, priorities, risks, and opportunities, with leadership able to make decisions based on reliable, current information.
 Built a strong operating rhythm across the global platform-level development team, with clear ownership, effective collaboration, and team members' skills deployed against the highest-priority fundraising opportunities.
 Improved coordination across platform, country, and program teams so that high-value proposals are prioritized appropriately, developed collaboratively, and submitted on time and at a consistently high quality.
 Established consistent CRM and pipeline management practices across the development function, with data being used to inform strategy, prioritization, and reporting.
 Created a well-organized, accessible library of standardized fundraising collateral and tools that enables fundraisers and country teams to move more quickly and consistently.
 Established effective feedback loops between funder and country-level intelligence, fundraising performance, and the organization's overall development strategy.
 Professional Experience 
 8+ years of experience across nonprofit fundraising/development, development strategy and/or development operations, including at least 5 years working directly within nonprofit or philanthropic fundraising. Candidates must demonstrate a deep practical understanding of the fundraising cycle, funder decision-making, proposal development and stewardship.
 Strong track record leading the development of complex philanthropic/grant proposals, ideally involving multiple programmes, geographies or internal stakeholders.
 Demonstrated experience turning frontline or field-level input into strategy and prioritization. 
 Demonstrated people-management experience, including coaching, performance management, setting priorities and allocating team capacity. Experience leading a distributed team is strongly preferred.
 Experience operating in a global or matrix organisation, with demonstrated ability to influence and coordinate country leaders, programme teams and other stakeholders who do not report directly to them.
 Comfortable using CRM and pipeline data to support fundraising decisions, forecasting and team management.
 Familiarity with the climate, clean energy, or entrepreneurship support landscape is a strong plus.
 Experience conducting dedicated funder-market or landscape research is advantageous.
 Personal Attributes 
 Structured, analytical thinker who is comfortable synthesizing messy, qualitative field input into clear recommendations.
 High level of adaptability in an environment with evolving team structures and workflows, with a genuine comfort operating in ambiguity - this means being a self-starter and embodying a growth mindset.
 High emotional intelligence — able to lead and support a development team well, build trust with country leads across diverse cultural contexts, and approach unfamiliar markets and norms with genuine curiosity and cultural sensitivity.
 Exceptional written communication skills — able to distill complex, multi-market fundraising intelligence into concise strategy and proposals.
 Strong project management skills; able to run a coordination function across concurrent proposals, deadlines, and stakeholders.
 Comfortable being an internal partner and "connective tissue" role rather than the primary external face of fundraising.
 Ability to work with a global team across time zones, with periodic travel for internal team meetings and relevant conferences/convenings.
 Proficiency in database/CRM management, Google Workspace, and Slack.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Foundational knowledge of global clean energy and climate change solutions and ecosystems and willingness to engage in in-depth self-learning on any gaps.
 Experience building or adding structure to a development operations function from an earlier, more informal stage.
 Due to the global nature of the organization and team, some meetings will take place outside of regular work hours.
 BENEFITS AND COMPENSATION
 This is a full-time remote position. Relocation assistance is not available for this role and compensation is competitive for the market the candidate is based in. Applicable benefits such as medical, dental, vision, paid time off, paid holidays and insurance will depend on the location of the selected candidate.

New Energy Nexus hires and promotes individuals on the basis of their qualifications for the job to be filled. We strongly encourage diverse applicants to apply.

About Flinks 
 Flinks is the embedded finance platform that brings together connectivity, intelligence, and payments — giving businesses the infrastructure they need to build and deliver seamless financial experiences at scale.
 As a leader in Open Finance in Canada, we’ve grown since 2016 into one of North America’s most trusted platforms for financial data access, enrichment, and money movement. We work with innovators across many industries, including lending, fintech, banking, insurance, and wealth management.
 Today, our platform connects to 15,000+ financial institutions across North America and powers over 1M monthly connections. We also give our customers unprecedented visibility into 4,500+ real-time financial insights to support smarter decisioning. Companies rely on Flinks to streamline onboarding, verify income, assess credit risk, and power faster payment experiences.
 We’re on a mission to drive financial innovation and help businesses build financial experiences that feel effortless, connected, and customer-first. That’s where you come in.
 The Role
 We're hiring our Senior Data Engineer (Data / ML Platform) to stand up data engineering as a discipline at Flinks . You'll own the data and ML platform that turns models into reliable production services, harden the data models the business runs on and close the seam between our data scientists and the product teams. This is a high-ownership, greenfield-leaning role: much of this foundation is yours to build and own, not inherit.
 If you like being the person who makes data and ML production-grade - pipelines, serving, governance, reliability - and you want broad impact across a company's data, this is built for you.
 What You'll Do
 Own and evolve the data platform - the BigQuery warehouse, dbt transformation layers, Airflow / Cloud Composer orchestration and Pub/Sub ingestion that feed every model and metric.
 Build and operate the ML platform - training pipelines (Kubeflow on Vertex AI), model serving (FastAPI behind Vertex endpoints), CI/CD, containerization and typed contracts. Take operational ownership of model-serving infrastructure so reliability isn't carried by the data scientists alone.
 Harden and standardize the data models the business depends on - improving schemas, fixing data-quality issues and establishing trustworthy source-of-truth feeds.
 Establish data governance and observability - bring data that lives outside the warehouse under proper governance and build operational metrics for products that don't yet have them .
 Standardize how data engineering is done across product lines - patterns, tooling and pipelines other teams can adopt.
 Partner across data science, backend and product on the producer to consumer contract (models produced by data science, consumed/aggregated downstream, surfaced to clients).
 What You'll Work On
 You'll help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' financial intelligence products, supporting everything from transaction enrichment and categorization to risk and payments decisioning.
 Key areas of focus include:
 Building scalable data pipelines that process and transform large volumes of financial data. 
 Designing and maintaining reliable datasets, data models, and feature pipelines used by machine learning and product teams. 
 Improving data quality, observability, and operational metrics across our platform and customer-facing products. 
 Developing cost-efficient, high-performance data services and infrastructure that support real-time and batch workloads. 
 Partnering closely with Data Science, Product, and Engineering teams to enable new capabilities and accelerate product delivery. 
 Contributing to the evolution of our data platform architecture as we continue to scale our products, customers, and machine learning capabilities.
 Our stack
 Python, SQL, Bash 
 Google Cloud Platform (GCP) 
 BigQuery and dbt 
 Airflow (Cloud Composer), Pub/Sub, and Cloud Functions 
 Kubeflow, Vertex AI, MLflow, and FastAPI 
 Docker, Terraform, and Protocol Buffers 
 Azure DevOps 
 Grafana and GCP Logging 
 You don't need experience with every tool listed above - strong Data Engineering fundamentals and experience building production data platforms matter more than direct experience with our exact stack. SQL is the exception : it's a non-negotiable (see Key Requirements). 
 Why This Role
 Greenfield ownership — help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' next generation of data and machine learning products. 
 High leverage impact — your work enables Data Science, Product, Engineering, and Risk teams to move faster with reliable, trusted data. 
 Real-world scale and complexity — work with large volumes of financial data powering products used by banks, fintechs, and financial institutions across North America. 
 Modern cloud-native environment — build on a modern GCP stack using contemporary data, platform, and machine learning tooling.
 Key Requirements
 Experience: 5+ years of hands-on Data Engineering experience designing, building, and operating production data platforms, pipelines, and warehouse solutions in a cloud environment.
 Data Engineering Expertise: Strong experience with ETL/ELT development, data modeling, schema design, orchestration, data quality, lineage, and warehouse optimization. Experience with BigQuery, dbt, Airflow, or equivalent modern data tooling is highly desirable.
 Technical Foundation: Expert SQL and strong Python skills, with the ability to build scalable, maintainable, and well-tested data solutions that support both operational and analytical workloads.
 Cloud Data Platforms: Experience working with modern cloud-native data ecosystems, including data warehouses, event-driven architectures, distributed processing, and platform observability.
 Operational Excellence: Demonstrated ownership of production systems, including monitoring, reliability, performance tuning, cost optimization, incident response, and ongoing platform improvements.
 Machine Learning Platform Exposure: Experience supporting machine learning workflows, feature pipelines, model-serving infrastructure, or MLOps environments is an asset, but a strong Data Engineering foundation is the primary requirement.
 Collaboration: Ability to partner effectively with Data Science, Product, Engineering, and QA teams to deliver trusted, scalable, and well-governed data solutions.
 Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
 Work Authorization: Must be legally authorized to work in Canada.

 Chef de file de la finance ouverte (Open Finance) au Canada, nous avons connu une croissance soutenue depuis 2016 pour devenir l’une des plateformes les plus fiables en Amérique du Nord en matière d’accès aux données financières, d’enrichissement des données et de mouvement de fonds.  Standardiser les pratiques d’ingénierie des données à travers les différentes lignes de produits — modèles, outils et pipelines pouvant être réutilisés par les autres équipes. 
 Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de science des données, de développement backend et de produit afin de définir et maintenir le contrat entre producteurs et consommateurs de données (modèles produits par la science des données, consommés ou agrégés en aval et exposés aux clients).

 BigQuery et dbt

 Job Description: 
 Primary Purpose   
 The Residence Life Co-ordinator (RLC) is responsible for ensuring the effective delivery of the student experience within an assigned student residence(s). This position acts as an advisor and support to students living in residence with emphasis placed on a student’s holistic development. The RLC provides leadership to Residence Life Staff (e.g. Dons) in the development of a diverse community based on individual rights, freedoms and responsibilities.   
 The RLC is part of an interdependent and collaborative team committed to integrating the student voice and connecting research and evaluation to our practice in order to continuously build on our understanding of our students' wants and needs and on our knowledge of how living environments contribute to student success. Our curricular approach facilitates the design and delivery of experiences and services so that students achieve priority developmental and educational outcomes.   
 Key Accountabilities   
 Student Support and Case Management   
 Engages with students who present with a variety of personal and/or transitional challenges related to their integration into the residence community and University setting.   
 Builds rapport with students within case management portfolio and supports students in connecting to on-campus and/or off-campus resources.   
 Executes the administration of the conduct process across residences through appropriate application of residence policy and procedures.   
 Facilitates student conduct processes and management of student issues (example: drug and alcohol infractions, roommate challenges, behavioral issues, etc.).   
 Facilitates educational conversations, and issues appropriate restorative or educational sanctions, in accordance with the Case Management Strategy.   
 Leads difficult conversations with students who experience challenges related to mental health, substance use, sexual violence, homesickness, isolation, academic stress, etc.   
 Responds to various levels of human crisis, such as self-harm, thoughts of suicide, disclosure of sexual violence, anxiety attacks, etc.   
 Demonstrates knowledge of emergency response procedures; problem solves, uses resources, and acts quickly in difficult situations.   
 Maintains confidential records of students within case management portfolio using internal database.   
 Collaborates with Case Support Coordinators to manage complex and critical student cases.   
 Ensures the rights of individuals as well of the community are upheld through appropriate use of policy and regulation.   
 Residence Life Coordinator’s supporting the Undergraduate portfolio will assume regular, rotating on call shift with peers and respond to urgent matters accordingly.   
 Supervision and Human Development   
 Provides day-to-day guidance, direction, and oversight to 10-18 Residence Life Dons in the development of a positive residence community.   
 Effectively supervises and supports Residence Life Don Team Leaders by providing day-to-day guidance, direction, and oversight.   
 Participates in and make decisions regarding the recruitment and training of student-staff positions.   
 Provides leadership in student-staff meetings and communicates regularly with the Manager, Residence Life with regard to student-staff and student concerns while upholding the confidentiality of the Department, staff and students.   
 Completes performance evaluations for direct reports and provides ongoing developmental feedback and coaching between evaluations.   
 Supports student-staff by redirecting individual and community actions or concerns towards restorative and educational initiatives that contribute to an atmosphere of accountability and responsibility.   
 Role models visibility, availability, and approachability with all staff, student-staff, and students, which includes engaging in evening and weekend responsibilities with the community.   
 Meets on a biweekly basis with student-staff and supports the execution of weekly team meetings.   
 Community Development & Program Administration   
 Contributes to the delivery of Student Development and Residence Experience’s (SDRX) programs and services so that students achieve priority developmental and educational outcomes.   
 Establishes and promotes a safe and healthy community within their assigned residence area. This includes organizing and prioritizing effective management of student experience operations.   
 Understands the needs of students in residence and ensures that programming facilitates community engagement across residence.   
 Provides leadership to all student-staff as they create, execute, and evaluate intentional programs. Ensures Don programs support student needs and student diversity.   
 Administers a community fund budget for the use of facilitating community building efforts for students and Dons. Submits expense reports for reconciliation purposes.   
 Oversees the spending of Don community funds and ensures accuracy of their budget reconciliation as required (e.g. twice per term).   
 Responds to and/or directs student inquiries in a timely manner. This includes forwarding maintenance concerns, facilitating room change requests, and providing referrals to additional campus resources.   
 Participates in and contributes to an assigned portfolio, which involves planning, executing, and assessing its effectiveness in residence. Assumes responsibility of additional portfolios as assigned by Manager, Residence Life.   
 Prioritizes consistency of program administration across all residence areas by collaborating and communicating with peers, direct reports, and Manager, Residence Life.   
 Training and Development   
 Coordinates the development and delivery of bi-annual student-staff training.   
 Remains knowledgeable and committed to student development theory and guiding principles within student affairs. Draws on these bodies of knowledge when coaching student-staff and students.   
 Encourages, organizes, and executes educational and developmental programs within residence to foster an atmosphere of personal development, academic enrichment, and community engagement.   
 Supports students and student-staff through their transition into the residence community and provides guidance and advisement to individuals for their own enrichment.   
 Contributes to an atmosphere of team and personal development by leading and supporting team-based initiatives, engaging in team projects, and supporting peers’ projects.   
 Interdepartmental Collaboration   
 Liaises with members of the department (e.g. Residence Services, Residence Learning, Residence Hospitality Experience, Maintenance & Security Services, Housing Occupancy & Marketing Services, etc.) and campus (e.g. Special Constable Services, Campus Wellness, Student Success Office, Office of Equity, Diversity, Inclusion & Anti-racism, Athletics, etc.) to facilitate the seamless execution of the student experience within residence.   
 Provides support to Housing department during regular end of term and start of term operations, including end of term room checks, managing move-in or move-out student issues, and supporting with building lock down processes between terms.   
 Required Qualifications   
 Education   
 Bachelor’s degree or equivalent education and experience   
 Experience   
 1-3 years’ experience in a full-time Student Affairs position, or equivalent   
 Experience supervising direct reports and managing difficult conversations   
 Experience training/mentoring student staff is required   
 Experience providing support to persons on matters related to mental health   
 Knowledge/Skills/Abilities   
 Proven ability to work autonomously with limited supervision   
 Demonstrated ability to work in a team-based environment and prioritize consistency   
 Strong oral and written communication skills   
 Effective presentation and meeting facilitation skills   
 Excellent coaching and conflict management skills   
 Demonstrated ability to remain calm in crisis response and exercise sound judgement   
 Vulnerable Sector Check required   
 Emergency First Aid & CPR A required

Document and Training Specialist – Radio Conjugate (RC) Pharmaceutical Quality Systems (PQS) 
 Location: Hamilton, ON 
 Onsite 5 days/ week 
 Fusion Pharmaceuticals, a member of the AstraZeneca Group, is a clinical-stage oncology
 company focused on developing next generation radio conjugates (RCs) as precision medicines.  Fusion has multiple pipeline programs entering early FIH trials. In addition, Fusion is pursuing combination programs between RCs and other therapeutic modalities including DNA Damage Response Inhibitors (DDRis) and immune-oncology agents. To support execution for these programs, Fusion has a fully operational Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliant innovative radio conjugate manufacturing facility to meet the demand for our growing pipeline of RCs.
 Position Summary 
 The Document and Training Specialist is an entry-level position within the Quality organization responsible for supporting the day-to-day administration of the controlled document management system and the learning management system (LMS). The role ensures that Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Work Instructions, policies, forms, and training curricula are accurately authored, reviewed, released, assigned, and tracked in accordance with Good Documentation Practices (GDP), ALCOA+ data integrity principles, and applicable GxP regulations (GMP, GCP, GLP, GVP as relevant to the business unit).
 This is an excellent opportunity for a diligent early-career professional to build a foundation in regulated-industry quality systems, working cross-functionally with subject matter experts, QA, Manufacturing, Regulatory Affairs, and Manufacturing Operations.
 Responsibilities 
 Document Lifecycle Support:  Process new documents, revisions, periodic reviews, and retirements within the electronic Document Management System (eDMS) (e.g., Veeva Vault QualityDocs, ensuring correct metadata, numbering, versioning, and workflow routing.
 Format and Quality Checks:  Review submitted documents against corporate templates and style guides for formatting consistency, correct references, hyperlink integrity, and adherence to GDP.
 Change Control Interface:  Link controlled document changes to associated change controls, deviations, or CAPAs in the QMS, and support impact assessments for documentation changes.
 Archival and Retention:  Maintain document archives in compliance with record retention schedules and regulatory requirements (e.g., 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11).
 Scanning and Filing: Ensure documentation are scanned, files in the document archive in a timely manner and all related activities have been completed.
 LMS Administration:  Create and maintain training items, curricula, and role-based  training matrices  in the LMS (e.g., ComplianceWire, SuccessFactors, Cornerstone, Veeva Vault Training); assign training upon document release and monitor completion.
 Training Assignment and Tracking:  Generate training assignments tied to job roles, monitor overdue training, and issue compliance reports to line managers and QA leadership.
 New Hire Onboarding Support:  Coordinate GxP onboarding training for new employees and contractors, ensuring role-based curricula are assigned prior to independent task performance.
 Training Records Integrity:  Ensure training records are complete, accurate, contemporaneous, and audit-ready in line with  ALCOA+ principles .
 Audit and Inspection Support:  Retrieve documents and training records to support internal audits, sponsor audits, and health authority inspections (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA, etc.).
 Metrics and Reporting:  Compile monthly targets for document cycle times, training compliance rates, and overdue actions, and support management review data preparation.
 Process Improvement:  Find opportunities to streamline document and training workflows and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives within the Quality function.
 Qualifications 
 Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Chemistry, Biology, Engineering, Information Management, Business Administration, or a related field. Advance degree is an asset.
 2-5 years of relevant experience; internships, co-op placements, or academic projects in a regulated environment (pharmaceutical, biotech, medical device, clinical research) are highly valued.
 Experience in GxP training, QMS, and document control within regulated life sciences (clinical/R&D and/or GMP), including hands‑on audit/inspection support and validated eDMS/eLMS operations an asset.
 Exposure to GxP environments (GMP, GCP, GLP, GVP) through coursework, internship, or prior role.
 Familiarity with electronic Document Management Systems (eDMS) or Learning Management Systems (LMS) such as Veeva Vault, MasterControl, ComplianceWire, or SuccessFactors, an asset.
 Basic understanding of change control, deviation management, and CAPA processes.
 Organizational Skills: Ability to manage multiple concurrent requests, prioritize under deadlines, and maintain meticulous records.
 Ability to stand for longer periods of time and lift up to 40 lbs.
 May require up to 10% travel, if applicable
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Familiarity with electronic Document Management Systems (eDMS) or Learning Management Systems (LMS) such as Veeva Vault, MasterControl, ComplianceWire, or SuccessFactors.
 Awareness of 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and ICH Q10 principles.
 Experience with data visualization or reporting tools (Power BI, Tableau) is a plus.
 Experience preparing for commercialization is advantageous.
 Systems: Strong technical experience with Veeva Vault (eQMS/eDMS) and UL ComplianceWire (eLMS) preferred; proficiency with Microsoft 365; familiarity with electronic signatures and Part 11/Annex 11 controls.
 Knowledge: Solid understanding of GxP regulations and data integrity (ALCOA+); awareness of manufacturing and QC workflows; working knowledge of integration with change control, deviation, CAPA, and risk processes.
